articles.title: 27 years, one painful goodbye: Suzy Kolber reveals why ESPN’s silence became the hardest part of her emotional exit
articles.summary: NFL News: Suzy Kolber gave ESPN 27 years. She was there for the launch of ESPN2. She was the first name attached to the X Games. She helped carry Monday Night F.
articles.body: Suzy Kolber gave ESPN 27 years. She was there for the launch of ESPN2. She was the first name attached to the X Games. She helped carry Monday Night Football when it moved to the network. When the layoffs came in 2023, she saw it coming. What she did not see coming was the part that broke her: ESPN was not going to say a single word about her leaving.Why did Suzy Kolber's ESPN exit hurt more than just losing her job?ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro had already warned Kolber about a week before the cuts were announced. He told her directly, "Suzy, there's a whiteboard and your name's on it." She processed it. She braced herself. She sat at her kitchen table with her daughter and said, "I think this is really happening."None of that was easy. But it was manageable, in the way that people find a way to manage things they can see coming. What caught her off guard was what came next.She found out that ESPN planned to make no public statement about her departure. No acknowledgment, no thank-you, not even a brief mention of someone who had been one of the most visible people at the network for nearly three decades. That is when it really hit her."Probably the most emotional thing was Norby saying to me [ESPN was] not going to say anything. I was the first person hired for the launch of ESPN2. I was the first person assigned to the X Games. I was part of Monday Night Football's move to ESPN. I was part of some pretty big franchises," Kolber said during an appearance on Richard Deitsch's Sports Media podcast."I was like, 'You're not gonna say a word? Not thanks for 27 years. Just acknowledge it?'"So she took it into her own hands. She wrote her own announcement, reached out to Adam Schefter and longtime ESPN PR executive Chris LaPlaca to help amplify it, and posted it herself. The moment it went live, something inside her gave way."As soon as I saw [the post] go live, I had a good three to five minutes of full-on sobbing," she said. "It was real."What did Suzy Kolber say during her final call with ESPN's Norby Williamson?The call that officially ended her ESPN career came from former executive Norby Williamson. At some point in the conversation, Williamson reminded Kolber that speaking negatively about the network could have consequences.She did not take that quietly."I have been the ultimate good soldier. All the [expletive] I've seen, I have never said one negative thing about this company. Like, do you think I'm going to start now?" she pushed back.It is a line that says a lot about how Kolber carried herself through 27 years. She had seen plenty. She stayed quiet through all of it. And even in the room where they were letting her go, her first instinct was not anger toward ESPN. It was defense of her own record.That kind of loyalty, met with institutional silence on the way out, is what made this story land the way it did for people. It was not really about a firing. It was about what happens when an organization forgets that the people who built it were actually people.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Texans LB Azeez Al-Shaair fined for writing 'Hind Rajab' on eye black in loss to Bills to honor killed Palestinian girl
articles.summary: Azeez Al-Shaair had been previously fined for writing 'Stop the Genocide' on his eye black last season.
articles.body:
Houston Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was fined more than $11,000 for an unauthorized message written on his eye black in their 36-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.

Al-Shaair was fined $11,492 on Tuesday, along with three other Texans for various infractions, according to KPRC2's Aaron Wilson . Al-Shaair wrote "Hind Rajab" across his eye black in a nod to a 5-year-old Palestinian girl who was killed by the Israeli military in 2024.

The fine was not due to the pro-Palestinian message specifically. Al-Shaair would have been fined by the league for any unauthorized message written on his eye black, as that is a violation of NFL rules. Other players across the league were also fined for equipment-related infractions in Week 1, including David Montgomery for an unauthorized logo on his cleats and Trent Brown for socks that didn't cover his lower leg, for example.

The Israel Defense Forces acknowledged for the first time last month that it opened fire on the vehicle that was carrying Rajab in Gaza in January 2024, according to CNN . She was one of seven family members traveling in a vehicle in northern Gaza when they came under Israeli fire, according to the report.

Rajab initially survived, and could be heard in a recording of a phone call to Palestinian responders begging for them to come and rescue her while she was trapped in the car with her dead relatives. An ambulance dispatched to save her later came under fire. Rajab was found dead 12 days later. The Israeli military initially denied involvement in the killing before acknowledging last month that it did open fire on the vehicle after a criminal investigation into the incident was opened.

Al-Shaair has been fined for writing messages on his eye black in the past. He was hit with a similar fine last season after writing "stop the genocide" on his eye black in the team's wild-card win over the Pittsburgh Steelers last season. He said after that game that he knew what he was doing and that a fine would be coming, but he didn't care.

"At the end of the day, it's bigger than me, the things that are going on," Al-Shaair said . "It makes people uncomfortable, imagine how those people feel. I think that's the biggest thing. I have no affiliation, no connection to these people other than the fact that I'm a human being. If you have a heart, then you are a human being and you can see what's going on in the world and check yourself real quick. When I'm walking off this field, that's the type of stuff that goes through my head that I have to check myself when I'm sitting here crying about football when there's people dying every day."

Al-Shaair had a team-high eight tackles in their loss to the Bills on Sunday at NRG Stadium. The 29-year-old had 103 total tackles and two interceptions last season while earning the first Pro Bowl nod of his career.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs battery case: Victim’s lawyers make major move to protect privacy as sealed evidence draws attention
articles.summary: NFL News: The legal chapter surrounding Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs took a significant turn Tuesday when attorneys representing the woman at the .
articles.body: The legal chapter surrounding Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs took a significant turn Tuesday when attorneys representing the woman at the center of his battery case filed a motion to seal evidence. The move came days after Jacobs pleaded no contest last Thursday to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges, both tied to a May incident involving his then-girlfriend. With the criminal phase largely settled, the focus has now shifted from the courtroom to what the public may or may not get to see.Why are the victim's lawyers trying to seal evidence in the Josh Jacobs case?Attorneys Ramses Jalalpour and Amir Tahmassebi stated Tuesday that "the motion is consistent with our client's desire to protect her privacy, particularly in light of Mr. Jacobs taking responsibility for his actions in the criminal proceeding."That framing matters. The lawyers are not contesting the outcome or disputing what happened. They are, specifically, drawing a line around how much of the surrounding documentation becomes public record. The motion targets a wide range of materials. The woman sought to seal police and supplemental reports, dispatch records, recordings, photographs, witness statements, investigative notes, forensic materials, medical or treatment-related information, and digital evidence.Her reasoning was stated plainly in the supporting brief. She wanted "only to prevent unnecessary public disclosure of information that identifies or locates her, reveals intimate details of the victimization or creates a material risk of further harm to her."One piece of evidence in particular has drawn attention: surveillance footage from the garage camera system, which police said corroborated the woman's account of what happened. That video has not been released. Given the motion now formally in place, it may never become public.What happens to Josh Jacobs now? His NFL future and pending suspensionJacobs, a three-time Pro Bowler, currently sits on the NFL's commissioner's exempt list, which keeps him away from playing and practicing while allowing him to continue receiving his paycheck. He can access team facilities for meetings, individual workouts, therapy, and rehabilitation.On the legal side, Jacobs was ordered to pay a $1,000 fine plus court costs following the no-contest plea. Under the agreement with prosecutors, the criminal damage charge could be dropped within a year, provided he stays out of trouble, avoids contact with the victim, completes counseling, submits to supervision, and pays restitution.The criminal case is functionally resolved. The NFL's response, however, is not. Jacobs could still face a league suspension, and with the exempt list status already in effect, Green Bay's offensive backfield has been operating without its starting running back before Week 1 of the new season has barely settled.The league has not publicly committed to a timeline, which leaves the Packers in an uncomfortable holding pattern. Whether the sealed evidence affects how the NFL conducts its own internal review remains to be seen. But the request itself signals that, for the woman involved, getting through this with some measure of privacy intact is the only thing that matters now.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bills get major advantage with Lions' 2 star safeties out
articles.summary: Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch are out for a Lions defense that ranks last against the pass after Week 1.
articles.body:
Josh Allen carved up last year's No. 1 defense to open the season.

He'll face the NFL's worst pass defense through one week of 2026.

And the Detroit Lions will still be missing two of their best defensive players.

Star safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch will both miss Thursday night's game against the Buffalo Bills at new Highmark Stadium.

Joseph and Branch opened the season on the physically unable to perform list, making them ineligible to return for the first four games.

It's good news for the Bills , whose passing attack that is off to a fast start.

Allen completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns in Buffalo's 36-31 victory over the Houston Texans .

Detroit had a much different opening weekend.

New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough completed 35 of 56 passes for 410 yards and three touchdowns in the Lions' 31-30 overtime victory. Detroit is last in the NFL with 378 net passing yards allowed.

Joseph, 25, was one of the NFL's best ballhawks before a knee injury derailed his 2025 season. He led the league with nine interceptions in 2024, earning first-team All-Pro honors, and has 20 interceptions in 55 career games.

Detroit rewarded Joseph after that season with a four-year, $86 million contract extension. Joseph's knee limited him to six games last season before he landed on injured reserve. The injury continued to linger into 2026, and he opened the season on PUP.

Branch, 24, made the Pro Bowl in 2024 after recording 109 tackles, 16 passes defended and four interceptions. He had 75 tackles, 2.5 sacks and nine passes defended in 12 games last season before tearing his Achilles against the Dallas Cowboys in December.

articles.title: ‘Biggest Ego in the League,’ ‘Absolute Madman’ — NFL Fans React to Ben Johnson’s ‘Disrespectful’ Admission After Bears’ 59-Point Eruption vs. Panthers
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears were major winners in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. If their latest game is any indication, the team will be very difficult to stop.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears were major winners in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. If their latest game is any indication, the team will be very difficult to stop. The Bears put up 59 points, the most in the league, in the NFL's opening week.

Head coach Ben Johnson, who has built a reputation as one of the best offensive minds in football, breathed new life into Chicago when he made his head coaching debut last season. Now, he is looking to cement the Bears as one of the best teams in all of football.

However, he does have his critics. Some fans aren't fans of how he carries himself. This became even more apparent when his recent comments went viral online.

Ben Johnson Hints He Wanted 60 Points Against Panthers

Johnson appeared on ESPN 1000 Chicago on Monday, September 14. He spoke about his team's big win over the Carolina Panthers, and the offensive onslaught his team produced to start the season.

In this appearance, Johnson made an admission about the game. He hinted that he considered a two-point attempt to push his team to 60 points in the win.

When the radio host mentioned thinking about a two-point try, Johnson remarked , "I don't think you were the only one."

Bears fans likely love this sort of comment. The aggressive mindset on offense made Johnson an in-demand head-coaching candidate when he ran the Detroit Lions offense. It's no surprise to see him take that same mindset and apply it to his work with Chicago.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

However, admitting to something like this after a blowout win does carry the risk of rubbing people the wrong way. That is exactly what happened, as many football fans took issue with this comment.

"Biggest ego in the league. He needs to be humbled," one fan said on social media.

"It's going to come back to bite him. The NFL isn't a league that rewards showing teams up," another fan said .

"Absolute piece of [expletive]. I want to see his pretty boy reaction when a team rams the score up his [expletive]," a third fan wrote in rather blunt terms .

Time will tell whether Johnson receives the humbling that these fans want to witness. For now, the Bears head coach has the right to gloat. He has earned some bragging rights over the last year.

Johnson took the Chicago head coaching job before the 2025 campaign. After a bit of a slow start, Chicago went on quite a run. The Bears won the NFC North and defeated the Green Bay Packers in the NFC Wild Card Round.

Chicago's playoff run ended in the Divisional Round. However, it gave the city plenty of reasons to believe in Johnson. His connection with Caleb Williams is clear to see. The future possibilities are tantalizing, to say the least.

It will certainly be interesting to see which team can take Bears down this year. Chicago will look for a second straight win on September 20 when they take on the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs’ ex-girlfriend makes major legal move as NFL seeks access to crucial evidence in Packers RB case
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs’ former girlfriend has made a major legal move by asking a Wisconsin court to permanently seal evidence connected to the case involving the Green...
articles.body:
Josh Jacobs ' former girlfriend has made a major legal move by asking a Wisconsin court to permanently seal evidence connected to the case involving the Green Bay Packers running back.

The motion was filed on Tuesday by attorneys representing the woman, identified in court documents as ANM, with the request centred on protecting her privacy.

The development comes just days after Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges following a May 23 incident at his residence.

NFL reportedly wants access to video in Josh Jacobs case

According to the filing, ANM's attorneys want sensitive records and discovery materials kept from public release. Their statement said the motion was "consistent with our client's desire to protect her privacy, particularly in light of Mr. Jacobs taking responsibility for his actions in the criminal proceeding."

The request could also have implications for the NFL, which is conducting its own investigation into the case.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport has reported that the league is seeking surveillance video from the incident. According to the criminal complaint, footage exists from inside Jacobs' garage.

Jacobs was initially arrested after police responded to a disturbance complaint on May 23. He was later booked on five counts, including felony strangulation/suffocation and misdemeanour charges of battery, criminal damage to property, disorderly conduct and intimidation.

The case was reduced before Jacobs' September 10 court appearance. He pleaded no contest to battery and criminal damage to property, receiving a $1,000 fine for the battery charge.

He also received a one-year deferred judgment agreement for the property-damage charge. The conditions include counselling, no contact with ANM, supervision and restitution.

Jacobs has remained on the NFL's Commissioner Exempt List since August 30 and cannot play or practise while the league reviews the case.

ANM's attorneys have argued that releasing the evidence could threaten her privacy, dignity and safety. A judge has yet to rule on the request for permanent sealing, although a temporary injunction was granted on September 10.

For Jacobs and the Packers, the NFL investigation now remains the next major development, with the league's access to the evidence potentially affected by the court's decision.

articles.title: NFL Hands Down Punishment for Play Involving Bills QB Josh Allen
articles.summary: The NFL is fining Houston Texans defensive lineman Mario Edwards for a hit on Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen. The post NFL Hands Down Punishment for Pl...
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen took a low hit in the team's win over the Houston Texans on Sunday, and now the NFL is handing down punishment for the play.

The Bills prevailed in a shootout, winning 36-31 thanks to the heroics of Allen and a few well-timed stops from the otherwise overmatched defense. The Texans defense had trouble slowing Allen, who accounted for all four touchdowns in the win.

Texans defensive lineman Mario Edwards not only left the game with a loss, but also took a financial penalty for a low hit on Allen in the third quarter. The penalty helped push the Bills in range for a field goal.

Edwards has already been penalized by the league for the infraction. The Spotrac transaction wire showed on Tuesday that the Texans linebacker was fined $8,923 for the roughing-the-passer penalty against Allen.

Edwards was not the only Texans player to earn a fine for the game. The transaction wire showed that three other players — running back David Montgomery , right tackle Trenton Brown , and linebacker Azeez Al-Shaiir — were all fined for uniform violations.

Though Allen had been tormented by the Texans defense in past years — and the Bills had not won a game in Houston in more than two decades — the Bills quarterback made easy work of their secondary on Sunday.

Allen threw for 334 yards and two touchdowns and added another two rushing touchdowns.

The Bills quarterback is already earning some MVP buzz. Former NFL quarterback turned commentator Russell Wilson predicted that Allen would add a second MVP trophy to his case by the end of the season.

"I think that he has a definite chance to win it," Wilson said on "Set Hut!" "I'm calling it out that he's probably gonna win it this year, because I think he knows it's time for the Buffalo Bills. New stadium … new coach. Obviously, the coach has been with him in Joe Brady, but I think it's gonna make a difference this year."

The Bills have a big test this week, facing a Detroit Lions team on short rest. The Bills will host the first-ever game at the new Highmark Stadium on Thursday night, a showdown between two of the league's best offenses.

Like the Bills defense, the Lions struggled in a 31-30 overtime win over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. They blew a 21-0 second-half lead, winning only when the stoped the Saints on a two-point conversion attempt in overtime.

Allen will get to face a depleted secondary, with the Lions placing starting safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph on the reserve/PUP list to start the season.

articles.summary: Azeez Al-Shaair faces an $11,492 NFL fine for writing Hind Rajab's name on his eyeblack during the Houston Texans' opener against the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body: Houston Texans middle linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair will be fined $11,492 by the NFL for breaking the league's rules on "personal messages" because he inscribed the name of a Palestinian girl on his eyeblack in tribute to her memory during Sunday's regular-season opener against the Buffalo Bills. Al-Shaair, who is Muslim, wrote the name of Hind Rajab on his eyeblack during the 36-31 loss to the Bills and kept it on even as reporters entered the Texans locker room to interview players afterward. The NFL sent Al-Shaair a letter saying he was in violation of Rule 6, Section 4, Article 8 of the rulebook. NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE MESSAGING WHILE BATTLING DOMESTIC ABUSE, DRUNK DRIVING AND PROSTITUTION ARRESTS The rule: "Throughout the period on game day that a player is visible to the stadium and television audience (including in pregame warmups, in the bench area, and during postgame interviews in the locker room or on the field), players are prohibited from wearing, displaying, or otherwise conveying personal messages either in writing or illustration, unless such message has been approved in advance by the League office." The NFL did not approve of Al-Shaair, or any player, wearing a personal tribute to Rajab on Sunday. What makes Al-Shaair's decision to wear the five-year-old girl's name on his equipment controversial is that practically all things involving Gaza and Israel are charged with emotion for Muslims and Jews and their respective supporters. Muslims view Rajab as a martyr who was killed at the hands of the Israeli Defense Forces in Gaza City in January 2024. People like Al-Shaair view Rajab's death as evidence that Israel is waging a genocide against the Palestinians in Gaza. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The IDF, meanwhile, maintains the killing was a horrible mistake amid the fog of war. That war, by the way, started when Hamas attacked Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, and killed approximately 1,200 men, women, and children and took others hostage. In August, the IDF acknowledged that its troops had fired at the vehicle carrying Rajab, her aunt, uncle and four cousins. Although Rajab survived that attack, a Red Crescent ambulance that appeared on the scene was also fired upon and 12 days later the bodies of Rajab, her family and two men from the ambulance were recovered. The IDF ordered a criminal investigation. Israeli media outlets Ynet and The Times of Israel reported that the IDF’s internal review said the car had approached Israeli positions while traveling against an announced evacuation direction. PRO-PALESTINE PROTESTER WHO INTERRUPTED SUPER BOWL LIX HALFTIME SHOW FOUND GUILTY IN COURT Al-Shaair clearly intended to send an anti-Israel message with his Rajab inscription and it is not the first time. In January, the linebacker was fined $11,593 for wearing eyeblack on which he inscribed the slogan "Stop the Genocide." These fines, by the way, are something of a pittance for Al-Shaair. He signed a three-year contract extension worth $54 million in the offseason. The contract included a $14 million signing bonus. Players subject to NFL accountability measures receive a letter informing them of what they did, a video of the play in question if that applies, why they are being fined, and how much it will cost them. They also receive information on how to appeal the fine. If they choose not to appeal, the fine is withheld from their next game check. If a player protests a ruling, he schedules a hearing with the NFL, and his case is assigned to one of the league’s current appeals officers. articles.title: Latest NFL Odds and Picks Factoring in New Weather Forecasts for Week 2 Schedule
articles.summary: Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season was a wild one, with several unexpected results littering the scoreboards. Of course, Week 1 is often unpredictable because some teams exit the preseason better prepared than others.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season was a wild one, with several unexpected results littering the scoreboards. Of course, Week 1 is often unpredictable because some teams exit the preseason better prepared than others.

In theory, fans should have a little more clarity on which teams are good and which are not entering Week 2. Of course, some of what we saw during the opening schedule will inevitably turn out to be a mirage.

Weather, while typically milder this time of year, is another X-factor that could impact the Week 2 schedule.

Here, you'll find a look at what you need to know for Week 2, including forecast information from The Weather Channel .

Carolina Panthers (-1.5) at Atlanta Falcons (Retractable Roof)

New Orleans Saints (+8.5) at Baltimore Ravens

Minnesota Vikings (+5.5) at Chicago Bears

Cincinnati Bengals (+3) at Houston Texans (Retractable Roof)

Pittsburgh Steelers (+4.5) at New England Patriots

Green Bay Packers (-3.5) at New York Jets

Cleveland Browns (+8.5) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Forecast: Scattered Showers, High of 89°F

Philadelphia Eagles (-7) at Tennessee Titans

Jacksonville Jaguars (+2.5) at Denver Broncos

Forecast: Isolated Thunderstorms, High of 71°F

Las Vegas Raiders (+7) at Los Angeles Chargers (Dome)

Seattle Seahawks (-4.5) at Arizona Cardinals (Retractable Roof)

Washington Commanders (+3.5) at Dallas Cowboys (Retractable Roof)

Miami Dolphins (+13.5) at San Francisco 49ers

Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Kansas City Chiefs

New York Giants (+7.5) at Los Angeles Rams (Dome)

Week 2 should go a long way toward confirming or disputing what we saw in Week 1. On Sunday night, for example, the Kansas City Chiefs will battle the Indianapolis Colts in a game that could say a lot about multiple teams.

The Chiefs looked like they could once again contend for a Super Bowl while throttling the Denver Broncos on Monday night. However, Denver simply may have been sluggish coming out of the preseason and playing on the road.

The only things we know for certain about Kansas City right now are that running back Kenneth Walker III is an elite offensive weapon, while quarterback Patrick Mahomes is healthy. Mahomes made the latter point clear with an early 15-yard touchdown run.

"That was definitely the moment, physically, to say all this work has paid off," Mahomes told reporters .

The Colts, meanwhile, were rolled by the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1. Is Indianapolis really that bad, or are the Ravens that good? We'll have some clarity after the Sunday night matchup and after Baltimore battles a New Orleans Saints team that just took the Detroit Lions to overtime.

The Lions, likewise, will have plenty to prove against the Buffalo Bills in Thursday night's opener. Detroit's defense struggled to contain Saints quarterback Tyler Shough and will certainly have its hands full with Josh Allen in Buffalo.

The good news for Detroit, which plays in a dome, is that weather shouldn't be a factor in Week 2. There's a chance of rain, but it currently appears low.

Other teams will be less fortunate. Rain could play a significant role in Chicago, Foxborough, and Tampa, while high heat could be a problem in Houston, Tennessee, and Arizona—though the Texans and Cardinals can close their roofs if the temperatures are too problematic.

Injuries could also be a factor this week, as the Seattle Seahawks, Atlanta Falcons, and Minnesota Vikings all suffered injuries at quarterback ahead of or during Week 1.

articles.title: Week 2 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Decisions for Fantasy Football Fringe Starters
articles.summary: Week 1 brought plenty of surprises to the fantasy football world, and it brought a few unfortunate injuries, too. This may leave many managers relying on fringe starters at key positions in Week 2.
articles.body:
Week 1 brought plenty of surprises to the fantasy football world, and it brought a few unfortunate injuries, too. This may leave many managers relying on fringe starters at key positions in Week 2.

The good news is that some matchups are favorable enough to allow second-tier fantasy starters to shine. Of course, picking the right matchups and properly projecting roles will be key.

And, there's obviously no guarantee that what we saw in Week 1 will translate into trends moving forward. Based on recent results, impending matchups, and a little educated guesswork, though, here's a look at some start/sit recommendations for point-per-reception (PPR) play in Week 2.

Start: Bhayshul Tuten, RB, Jacksonville Jaguars

The Jacksonville Jaguars battered the Cleveland Browns through the air early in Week 1, and despite building an early lead, they never leaned heavily on new starting running back Bhayshul Tuten. The second-year back did tally 88 scrimmage yards, but he logged just 15 carries, one reception, and no touchdowns.

It's clear that Liam Coen is likely to use a committee approach to his backfield more often than not this season.

However, Tuten still has an opportunity to reward fantasy managers this week in a potential playoff preview against the Denver Broncos. While Denver had one of the league's top defenses a year ago, it found few answers for the Kansas City Chiefs and running back Kenneth Walker III on Monday night.

Only the Carolina Panthers surrendered more fantasy points to opposing running backs than the Broncos in Week 1.

Sit: Travis Etienne Jr., RB, New Orleans Saints

Tuten is replacing 2025 starter Travis Etienne Jr. in Jacksonville's backfield, and Etienne was a legitimate fantasy star a season ago. However, his floor appears to be much lower now that he's with the New Orleans Saints.

To be fair, the Saints spent most of Week 1 playing from behind, so Etienne was never likely to get a ton of carries. However, the fact that he logged as many carries as Kendre Miller—and watched Miller get the goal-line work—is concerning.

Etienne did salvage the week with seven receptions, but he'll be difficult to trust this week against the Baltimore Ravens.

The Ravens are hoping for a defensive resurgence under new head coach Jesse Minter, and they just might get it. Despite facing star Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor in Week 1, the Ravens surrendered just 102 rushing yards, 251 total yards, and 23 points.

Taylor did have a pair of rushing touchdowns, but Miller's presence is problematic for Etienne managers.

Start: Emeka Egbuka, WR, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka had a solid, if unspectacular, 2026 debut, finishing with five catches for 63 yards. Even though the Bucs spread the ball around against the Cincinnati Bengals, Egbuka should be in store for a bigger Week 2 outing.

Tampa is set to host the Browns, who looked absolutely lost in trying to defend Jacksonville's passing attack on Sunday. Only the Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings surrendered more to opposing wide receivers in Week 1.

That's part of the equation here. The other piece is that this will be a revenge game for current Bucs signal-caller and former Browns quarterback Baker Mayfield.

"I mean, obviously, there's history there—there's no way to go around that," Mayfield told reporters (h/t ProFootballTalk's Myles Simmons ).

Expect the Buccaneers to air it out early and often, and for Egbuka to have a strong stat line.

Sit: Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

While Denver's defense looked nothing like the championship-caliber unit it was a year ago in Week 1, it did limit Kansas City's wide receivers. It's certainly worth recognizing that the Chiefs leaned heavily on the run, but it's also worth noting that the Broncos surrendered the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wideouts this past week.

Of course, the bigger issue for Jaguars wideout Brian Thomas Jr. may be the fact that he's no longer one of Trevor Lawrence's go-to targets. He did log three receptions and 40 yards in Week 1, but Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers are both more trustworthy options.

Washington has firmly entrenched himself as Jacksonville's new No. 1 receiver.

Jacksonville should try to lean on its ground game in Denver, just as the Chiefs did at home on Monday night. Thomas might break a big play, but he's unlikely to have a high target share and is a risky play against a defense desperate to return to form.

articles.body: Grow up near a noisy place, and no noise disturbs you. Grow up near a desert, and no sand irritates your eyes. Grow up in a humid environment, and no sweat droplet tickles your skin. You assume the place you grew up in won’t surprise you anymore. But in Josh Allen’s case, that isn’t true.While Josh Allen’s childhood on a California farm might suggest that outdoor creatures couldn’t unsettle the Buffalo Bills quarterback, that isn’t the case.A recent clip reminds fans that growing up around nature doesn’t necessarily mean loving every creature that comes with it. A spider showed up on the podium during his recent press conference, prompting him to say, “I don’t like that.”Josh Allen’s farm childhood shaped his toughness but he still doesn’t like spidersJosh Allen grew up in Firebaugh, California. His family has deep agricultural roots. They ran a large 3,000-acre farm, and Allen helped out while growing up. He drove a tractor, worked with crops like cotton, wheat, and cantaloupes, and moved irrigation equipment. He endured 115-degree heat while moving irrigation pipes, weeding, and picking crops.His farm-life upbringing and agricultural work earned him regional and national recognition through the National FFA Organization, including honors in diversified crop production and grain production entrepreneurship.That farm-life background has been a part and parcel of Allen’s story. Before becoming a popular NFL quarterback, he was a small-town California kid who was used to hard work and rural life. However, being accustomed to it is different from liking every part and parcel of the outdoors.When an eight-legged creature appeared on the podium during a press meet, he looked at it and said, “It’s a spider.”Took a brief pause, much like how one would take a brief pause before acting out in front of a wild creature out in the jungle or fauna of life.He was assessing where the spider was going next; if it came anywhere near him, he would have jumped or moved back a little. But the spider went the other way. After watching the eight-legged creature go the other way, Josh said, “I don’t like that.”Josh Allen assessed the spider’s movementJosh had kept his hands on the podium. After noticing the spider, he immediately moved his hands to his legs. After answering the reporter’s question, he avoided looking at it for as long as he could, then quickly glanced back to see if it had come toward him. That glance was beyond cute!Allen’s reaction made it clear that spiders aren’t exactly at the top of his list of favorite fauna. The contrast makes the moment highly entertaining. For someone who spent his childhood outdoors, around crops, machinery, and agricultural life, reacting with “I don’t like that” comes off as a surprise!His dislike for spiders says nothing about being uncomfortable with nature in general. Allen’s quick reaction simply highlights a personal preference. Someone can enjoy farm life, outdoor activities, and working around animals while still preferring to keep a little distance from eight-legged creatures like spiders.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Week 2 Waiver Wire Top Pickups and Drops After Evaluating Week 1 Box Scores
articles.summary: The opening slate of the NFL season is always an unpredictable one for fantasy football enthusiasts. While roles are easy to predict for top stars like Christian McCaffrey, Justin Jefferson, and Trey McBride, second-tier starters regularly surprise in Week 1.
articles.body:
The opening slate of the NFL season is always an unpredictable one for fantasy football enthusiasts. While roles are easy to predict for top stars like Christian McCaffrey, Justin Jefferson, and Trey McBride, second-tier starters regularly surprise in Week 1.

Things were certainly no different in this year's opening week. With players like A.J. Brown, Sam Darnold, and Kyler Murray suffering injuries during the week, many managers will be looking to adjust their lineups via the waiver wire.

Here, you'll find a look back at what transpired in Week 1, projected roles for Week 2, and some recommendations for players to drop or target on the waiver wire.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

After throwing for more than 400 yards with three touchdowns in Week 1, New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough is the most obvious waiver target at quarterback for Week 2. Managers who can land him via claims, though, should consider Miami Dolphins signal-caller Malik Willis.

Willis had a solid outing against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, finishing with 17.7 fantasy points. He's a capable dual-threat with a tremendous amount of upside, even if he faces a tough matchup against the San Francisco 49ers this week.

The 49ers largely held the Los Angeles Rams and quarterback Matthew Stafford in check last Thursday.

This won't be an ideal week to start Willis, but it's the perfect time to claim and stash him. He's currently rostered in just 32 percent of fantasy leagues.

Drop: Tyrone Tracy Jr., RB, New York Giants

Cam Skattebo is clearly the lead ball-carrier in the New York Giants' backfield. However, new head coach John Harbaugh is likely to use a committee approach throughout the 2026 season. This reality made backups Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy Jr. attractive handcuffs heading into Week 1.

Singletary, who logged four receptions and scored a touchdown in Week 1, is worth retaining. However, it's safe to drop Tracy.

The third-year back saw the field for just two offensive snaps against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. He did log carries on both of those reps, but he also fumbled on one of them.

Following a poor preseason and his latest gaffe, the Giants are highly unlikely to trust Tracy moving forward. Managers shouldn't trust him either, even as a handcuff.

Add: Kaelon Black, RB, San Francisco 49ers

There's a shortage of dependable fantasy backs this year, and managers simply aren't going to find quality starters on the waiver wire. However, 49ers backup Kaelon Black has a ton of upside as a rotational player in Kyle Shanahan's offense.

Christian McCaffrey is clearly San Francisco's starter, but Black recorded a catch and 70 scrimmage yards against the Rams on Thursday.

In addition to being one of the top handcuffs in the league this year, Black should have a high flex ceiling in games the 49ers are expected to win. They are widely expected to win big over the visiting Miami Dolphins this week, which could yield a sizeable workload for Black.

The rookie out of Indiana is rostered in only 21 percent of fantasy leagues.

Dehsuan Watson and the Cleveland Browns' passing offense were even worse than most expected during Sunday's blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. That's probably reason enough to abandon Jerry Jeudy, who has rapidly regressed since making the Pro Bowl in 2024.

Another reason to drop Jeudy is the emergence of rookie receivers K.C. Concepcion and Denzel Boston. The two were clearly the focal point of the Browns' offense on Sunday, and Jeudy finished with just two catches for 26 yards on four targets.

It's highly unlikely that Jeudy will return to Pro Bowl form in Cleveland, and he's certainly unlikely to do it this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

While the Bucs' defense surrendered 33 points to the Cincinnati Bengals, it held star receiver Ja'Marr Chase to just two catches and 12 yards.

D.J. Moore had a strong Buffalo Bills debut in Week 1, finishing with five catches for 110 yards and a touchdown. Tight end Dalton Kincaid, meanwhile, racked up five catches for 130 yards against the Houston Texans.

While Moore and Kincaid may be Josh Allen's go-to targets in 2026, there's room for Khalil Shakir in the passing attack. He wasn't as prolific against Houston but still finished with four catches and 50 yards on six targets.

Shakir and Kincaid tied for the second-most targets for Buffalo in Week 1 behind Moore's eight.

Shakir has flex value this week against a very suspect Detroit Lions secondary, and he has a very high season-long ceiling, given Kincaid's recent injury history. He's rostered in 59 percent of fantasy leagues, and it's worth seeing if he's still available in yours.

*Fantasy roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2
articles.summary: Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season brought a few twists, surprises, and, unfortunately, injuries. A team or two may consider turning to the trade market in response.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season brought a few twists, surprises, and, unfortunately, injuries. A team or two may consider turning to the trade market in response.

The November 10 trade deadline is still nearly two months away. We're still weeks away from truly knowing which teams are likely to be this year's biggest buyers and sellers. However, we may see our first big in-season trade soon, with trade activity only increasing from there.

Who are the best and most realistic trade targets heading into Week 2? That's what we're here to examine.

Here are our top 10 trade candidates, ranked by past production, upside, positional value, contract/cap implications, likely availability, and relevant recent rumors.

We'll also project trade values based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals, while providing some logical suitors for each player.

10. Brandon Aiyuk, WR, San Francisco 49ers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 7th-Round Pick

The San Francisco 49ers have been practically begging teams to bid on disgruntled wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk since the offseason began.

"We're available. Give us a call," general manager John Lynch told reporters in his post-draft press conference.

It's hard to envision San Francisco suddenly changing its stance on Aiyuk, even after promising rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suffered an ankle injury in the season opener. He's expected to miss at least a month, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Although Aiyuk hasn't played since suffering a significant knee injury in 2024, he is still only 28 and surpassed 1,300 receiving yards when he was last healthy in 2023. He could draw interest from teams who have experienced critical injuries at receiver.

Stribling, A.J. Brown, Ja'Kobi Lane, and Ladd McConkey were among the receivers who suffered injuries in Week 1.

Potential Suitors: Baltimore Ravens, New England Patriots

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 7th-Round Draft Pick

Quality defensive linemen are usually in demand, as injuries at the position make role players like Solomon Thomas even more valuable.

The Atlanta Falcons, for example, recently lost Da'Shawn Hand to a season-ending quad tear.

The Tennessee Titans acquired Thomas in an offseason trade with the Dallas Cowboys. Adding him made some sense, as it reunited Thomas with new Titans head coach Robert Saleh. However, Thomas will be a free agent in 2027. After getting blown out in Week 1, it's hard to imagine Tennessee becoming playoff-relevant before then.

Thomas probably isn't a starter at this stage of his career, but the 30-year-old recorded 27 tackles and three tackles for loss in a rotational role with Dallas last season.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Los Angeles Chargers

8. Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 2nd-Round Pick

The Jacksonville Jaguars aren't poised to be big-time sellers at the trade deadline. They thumped the lowly Cleveland Browns in their opener and could have a realistic shot at a Super Bowl push this season.

However, general manager James Gladstone has shown that he isn't afraid to make an aggressive trade if he believes it will benefit his squad. He traded starting corner Tyson Campbell in-season last year.

The Jags have dismissed the trade buzz surrounding wideout Brian Thomas Jr. However, it's fair to wonder how tightly they'll hang onto him now. Thomas had three catches for 40 yards in the opener, but Parker Washington has fully arrived as Jacksonville's new No. 1 receiver.

Washington is set to be a free agent in 2027. Moving Thomas, who will be extension-eligible in the spring, could help pave a financial path to paying Washington like a top-tier target.

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 3rd-Round Pick

No one expected the Browns to be particularly good in 2026. If Week 1 is an accurate indication, though, Cleveland is even worse than everyone thought. Deshaun Watson continues to look like a quarterback who can't get it done. Both Todd Monken and defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg appear to be in over their heads.

The Browns should be looking to chase 2027 draft capital in their pursuit of a quality quarterback. Starting corner Tyson Campbell could potentially bring some. He started 12 games for Cleveland last season and allowed an opposing passer rating of just 84.8 in coverage.

Campbell is also just 26 years old and under contract through 2028. With an annual salary of $19.1 million, he's on the pricier side, but he should interest contenders who need a cornerback.

Denzel Ward is the bigger name in Cleveland's cornerback room, but ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported in June that the Browns were totally uninterested in moving him.

Potential Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

6. Mason Rudolph, QB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick

Like the Jaguars, the Pittsburgh Steelers won their opener and are probably thinking more about a playoff run than the trade deadline. However, Pittsburgh also has a surplus of quarterbacks, with Mason Rudolph, Drew Allar, and Will Howard sitting behind starter Aaron Rodgers.

According to longtime NFL reporter Jason La Canfora, the Steelers are open to trading Rudolph if they can find a buyer.

"The one thing stopping this is not Pittsburgh's willingness to sell, it's the number of quarterbacks potentially available across the league which could make finding a deal more difficult," La Canfora wrote for Casino.org.

Other backups could be available, but teams also need depth and/or a spot starter. The Falcons have a quarterback mess on their hands. Over the past week, the Seattle Seahawks lost Sam Darnold to a hip injury. The Minnesota Vikings also lost Kyler Murray to a concussion.

Rudolph has 19 regular-season starts and one playoff start on his resume.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Seattle Seahawks

Projected Trade Value: 2027 1st-Round Pick, 2028 1st-Round Pick

The Las Vegas Raiders' 1-0 start to the season should cool any Maxx Crosby trade chatter for the immediate future.

Crosby did ask for a trade following the 2025 season. The Raiders did agree to trade him to the Baltimore Ravens in a deal that fell through. According to ESPN's Ryan McFadden , however, Las Vegas wasn't actively looking to move Crosby in the spring before Baltimore made an offer it couldn't turn down.

Of course, the Raiders aren't going to play the Miami Dolphins every week. At some point, they'll turn the offense over to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. If and when the Raiders start to stumble, building around Mendoza should become the central focus.

Moving a pass rusher like Crosby can help jump-start a rebuild, a reality that the Browns and Dallas Cowboys recently realized. The Raiders have realized it as well, as they would have already traded Crosby if the Ravens hadn't backed out of the deal.

Expect teams that need pass-rushing help to make more offers to acquire Crosby before the trade deadline passes.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, Dallas Cowboys

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick

The Browns traded Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in an effort to build for the future. Wide receiver Jerry Jeudy probably won't be part of that future. Rookies Denzel Boston and K.C. Concepcion are the new faces of Cleveland's receiving corps.

"Now, from what I've seen of Boston and Concepcion, Jeudy could be a real trade chip played by GM Andrew Berry at the November 10 deadline, if not earlier," Grossi said in August (h/t Max Dible of Heavy).

Boston and Concepcion became the focal point of the Browns' passing attack in Week 1, as Jeudy finished with just two catches for 26 yards on four targets. The 2024 Pro Bowler is unlikely to regain his status as a No. 1 target in Cleveland.

However, Jeudy is still only 27 years old and has a contract that should appeal to 2026 contenders in need of receiver help—he has a base salary of only $1.5 million . Given the injuries we've already seen at the position, Jeudy should have a deadline market if the Browns are reasonable with their asking price.

Potential Suitors: Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots

3. Kayvon Thibodeaux, Edge, New York Giants

The New York Giants announced their return to relevance with a 28-20 win over the rival Cowboys on Sunday Night Football . While they still have a long way to go to be considered NFC contenders, the Giants probably won't be selling off pieces in the near future.

However, the future of pass rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux remains murky at best. The 2022 first-round pick will be a free agent next offseason. New York has added other premier edge talent. Brian Burns and Abdul Carter lead the pass-rushing rotation, while rookie linebacker Arvell Reese could eventually transition to being an edge player.

Thibodeaux, meanwhile, appears to have become a pure rotation player under new head coach John Harbaugh. He played just 47 percent of the defensive snaps in Week 1, though he did log a quarterback hit.

It's always nice to have pass-rushing depth. At some point, however, the potential return in a trade will outweigh the value of having Thibodeaux as depth for the remainder of the season. If Thibodeaux can't carve out a more prominent role, the Giants can't expect to get a valuable compensatory pick by letting him walk in 2027 free agency.

2. Joey Porter Jr., CB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Theoretically, the Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. have time to sort out their differences and focus on the 2026 season. However, Porter wants a new contract. Pittsburgh has traditionally avoided contract talks after the regular season starts.

Porter was inactive in Week 1 and could be on the move in the not-too-distant future.

According to ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , "the possibility of a trade remains in play."

Porter might not be an elite cover corner, but he's been an above-average starter since midway through his rookie season. He'd be a strong fit for most cornerback-needy defenses, with the caveat that acquiring him would also require a lucrative new contract.

Christian Gonzalez leads all cornerbacks with a deal worth $33.8 million annually. It's fair to assume Porter wants a deal near the top of the market.

Potential Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders

The 49ers throttled the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1. They look like a team that could make a Super Bowl run in 2026. As long as that remains true, San Francisco will likely be even less inclined to move backup quarterback Mac Jones than it was during the offseason.

The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt reported that San Francisco was looking for a second-round pick in exchange for Jones during the spring.

Jones proved last year that he can keep the 49ers afloat if Brock Purdy misses time. He went 5-3 as a starter while throwing for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions in 2025.

The unknown is how long San Francisco will prioritize quarterback insurance over an intriguing return. Jones is practically guaranteed to depart in 2027 free agency. He could potentially net a big haul from a playoff hopeful in search of a starting quarterback. A conditional second-round pick that can become a first might be enough to get a deal done.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Minnesota Vikings

*Contract and cap information via Spotrac . Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference .

articles.title: Simone Biles is 50-50 on the 2028 Olympics but 100% certain about moving to Indianapolis for Jonathan Owens
articles.summary: NFL News: Simone Biles just finished building her dream home in Texas. Five years of planning, approvals, construction headaches, and custom everything -- and b.
articles.body: Simone Biles just finished building her dream home in Texas. Five years of planning, approvals, construction headaches, and custom everything -- and barely a year after moving in, she's packing up again. Not permanently, but still. Jonathan Owens signed a one-year deal with the Indianapolis Colts in March, his fifth NFL team, and Biles has already made her call: Indianapolis is home now too. She told PEOPLE at the 2026 US Open that the move is coming, just a little later than the start of the season.Is Simone Biles actually moving to Indianapolis full time?Not exactly full time, but it's more than a weekend visit. Speaking to PEOPLE on September 8, Simone Biles said she's been based in Houston for most of the season so far but has a firm plan to relocate."I've been in Houston most of the time, so I'm going to officially move there a little bit later," she said. "So I haven't experienced too much, but the stadium is stunning. It's beautiful. I'm just excited to watch my husband. It doesn't matter, as long as he's safe and healthy and he's having fun, then I don't care."The couple's main residence is still their custom-built waterfront mansion in Texas, which Biles only announced as complete in November 2025. But Owens' new contract means another city, another adjustment, and Biles is clearly not treating it as a burden. When Owens signed with the Colts back in March, she posted on Instagram almost immediately: "Excited to call Indy home this upcoming football season. Beyond proud of you @jowens! Keep defeating the odds, I love you."Why did Simone Biles leave her Texas dream home so soon after completing it?The timing is admittedly a bit ironic. Biles spent five years getting that house built -- the design process alone started in 2020 and took over a year. She waited on HOA approvals, broke ground in February 2022, and finally saw construction wrap on November 11, 2025. All that patience, and now she's splitting time with Indiana.But the bigger picture here is pretty straightforward. This couple moves together. Owens has played for the Cardinals, Texans, Packers, Bears and now the Colts. Biles has followed him through all of it, showing up on sidelines across the country with custom game-day fits and genuine enthusiasm. The Texas home was never really about being rooted in one place -- it was about having something permanent they built together, something to come back to.In May 2025, Biles told PEOPLE how much Owens was part of that process too: "I think we've done a good collab of what we wanted our house to look like."What happened at Jonathan Owens' first Colts game?Owens made his regular-season debut for Indianapolis on September 13 against the Baltimore Ravens, and Biles was there. Before kickoff, the two shared a pregame kiss on the sideline and ran through a handshake -- the kind of small, personal ritual that has become a signature of their public appearances together.It was a familiar scene, just in a new stadium. Biles had already been to Colts preseason games during August, showing up in custom blue-and-white looks built around Owens' No. 38 jersey. The sideline fashion has always been part of it -- she did the same thing in Chicago, building custom looks around Bears colors — but what actually stands out is how consistently she shows up, regardless of the city.What is Simone Biles' plan for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics?That's the question nobody can fully answer right now, including Biles herself. In an interview with CNN in April 2026, she put her chances at "50-50." She said she and her coaches believe she could get physically ready, but the physical side isn't the only variable. The mental and emotional commitment that another Olympic campaign demands is a different conversation.For now, Indianapolis is where her head is at -- literally.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Carson Wentz, J.J. McCarthy, Vikings' QB Situation Amid Kyler Murray Injury
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy is reportedly not expected to factor in as a potential starting quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2 against the Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy is reportedly not expected to factor in as a potential starting quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2 against the Chicago Bears.

According to ESPN's Dan Graziano , every indication is that Kyler Murray will start at quarterback on Sunday if he clears concussion protocol, and Carson Wentz will be the starter if Murray is not cleared in time.

Graziano added that rather than it being a negative reflection on McCarthy, the quarterback pecking order is a result of the Vikings being most comfortable with a veteran like Wentz to replace an injured starter during a game or to be prepared to start when there is uncertainty during the week because of injury.

If Murray is unable to suit up in Week 2, all signs point toward McCarthy serving as Wentz's backup.

Early in Minnesota's 39-22 win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, Murray took a hard hit that concussed him and knocked him out of the game.

Wentz took over and performed well, throwing for 133 yards, three touchdowns and no picks.

He had an especially strong connection with No. 1 wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who reeled in eight receptions for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the game.

After missing his entire rookie season due to a knee injury, McCarthy was Minnesota's primary starter last season. He posted a 6-4 record, but completed only 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, prompting the Vikings to look to improve the quarterback position.

Wentz is a highly experienced NFL quarterback with a career record of 49-49-1 to go along with 23,759 passing yards, 162 touchdowns and 72 interceptions.

Based on his performance in Week 1, Wentz seems like the quarterback who gives the Vikes the best chance to win while Murray is out, so it comes as little surprise that Wentz will likely be under center in Week 2 if Murray can't go.

articles.title: Cowboys' Caleb Downs Talks NFL Debut vs Giants, Rookie Season, Ohio State and More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Everything unfolded perfectly for Caleb Downs.
articles.body:
Everything unfolded perfectly for Caleb Downs.

The Dallas Cowboys rookie safety, playing in his first NFL regular-season game in front of a national audience on Sunday Night Football , lined up on the edge and had a clear blitzing lane toward New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart.

The end result was Downs unleashing a massive hit on Dart, forcing a fumble and announcing himself to the NFL world in primetime.

"He called the play, and I looked in the backfield and was like, 'I don't think there's anybody who is going to block me,'" Downs told Bleacher Report. "So then I just started running and was like, 'oh, I've got to get there.' Then I saw him pump fake the ball, and I was like, 'oh, it's over with.'" So yeah, I just tried to get the ball out as well as I could. I wish we could have gotten the turnover, but it was good."

It was part of a brilliant individual debut for the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NFL draft.

He was flying around the field throughout Sunday's game and finished with eight tackles, one sack and one forced fumble. He was also on the field for the majority of the defensive snaps and featured in coverage and against the run.

While the Cowboys lost 28-20, Downs was a bright spot for the team and its fans as they look ahead toward the future.

"It's hard to focus on my individual performance because we didn't complete the ultimate goal, but it was a good experience," he said. "Made some plays, did my job a lot of times. So that was cool to be able to do so on such a high level. But I'm really just looking forward to this next one and accomplishing the main goal as a team. I know what I did well, but it's all about improving and getting better."

There couldn't have been much more hype surrounding Downs ahead of his rookie season seeing how he was a star joining America's Team and a defensive unit that needed to make significant strides from last year.

All he did in college was help lead Alabama to the SEC championship and College Football Playoff as a freshman before transferring to Ohio State and elevating his game even more for the Buckeyes. He was a national champion, back-to-back All-American and the Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year during his time at Ohio State.

B/R's NFL Scouting Department ranked him as the best overall player in its big board of prospects leading up to the draft, and he fell to the Cowboys at No. 11 in part because safeties are not always as valued at the NFL level as positions such as quarterback, offensive tackle and wide receiver.

But his impact was clear right from the start, suggesting he is going to surpass even the sky-high expectations that were put in place.

His absence was also clear at the college level, as Ohio State blew a 20-point lead in the fourth quarter during Saturday's loss to Texas without him on the backend of the defense to provide a stabilizing force.

However, Downs believes his former team will be able to bounce back from the early setback just like his professional team.

"If we would have played a schedule like they have this year last year, we would have been tremendously better on the back end of the season," he said of Ohio State. "Yes, they lost, but at the end of the day playing against good teams is what makes you ready to win big games at the end of the season.

"That's a huge positive that they're going through. Being able to bounce back from a loss, especially a game like that where they had it in their hands and let it slip from their grasp, is something Coach Ryan Day and them are going to excel at. I'm excited to see how they respond."

Fortunately for Buckeyes and Cowboys fans, there is still a majority of the season to look forward to even after the early losses. And Downs is making sure those fans have the perfect snack for their tailgates as the campaign continues.

He partnered with Dot's for its "A Winning Season Tastes Like Dot's" campaign, which is celebrating the tradition of football fans coming together for a new year with the launch of its limited-time offering, Chipotle Honey Pretzels.

"It's been going really well," Downs said of the partnership. "'A Winning Season Tastes Like Dot's' hits home for me because whenever I'm watching a game or watching a movie and just chilling with the family, I'm always eating Dot's. So this worked out. Whenever I go to the movies, that's my first pick."

Chipotle Honey is his flavor of choice, and he said "they haven't left my sight."

Downs will surely continue to get off-the-field opportunities such as this one if he continues to play like he did in Sunday's opener.

Yet for as brilliant as he was, it is an understatement to say the first game did not go according to plan for the Cowboys. The defense that was last in the league in points allowed and 30th in yards allowed last season looked like it still had a number of issues, as Dart threw for 230 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions.

New York also ran for 165 yards and a touchdown, while even the talented Dallas offense didn't have a single player finish with more than 44 yards through the air or on the ground. Dak Prescott also threw a costly interception as the visitors struggled to generate any consistent momentum.

Still, it was just the first game for a team that has plenty of talent in place with Prescott, Javonte Williams, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, among others. It is reasonable to expect the offense to be among the league's best as the season progresses.

And while the defense is still a concern, having a young playmaker like Downs should lead to more improvement. He only figures to get better with more experience, which is a troubling thought for opposing offenses given how effective he was in his first game.

So why should Cowboys fans remain optimistic?

"I would just say perseverance," Downs said. "We have a very well-rounded team, and we know what we need to fix. That's what we're going to do. We're going to focus on the details, focus on the little things. That way next time we get on that stage, we can do what we need to do."

He also didn't feel overwhelmed by the speed of his first regular-season game and avoided any of the cliche welcome to the NFL moments that sometimes cause early issues for rookies.

"I would just say football is football," Downs said. "Whoever makes the least amount of mistakes and whoever doesn't beat themselves is usually going to win the game. So we have to go out and play our best game on Sunday."

Sunday will be another opportunity against a division rival in the Washington Commanders.

It will also be Downs' first regular-season home game of his career and an opportunity to immediately get back on track in front of a raucous crowd that should create plenty of energy. Washington is also coming off a 5-12 season and lost its opener to the Philadelphia Eagles.

"I'm expecting a lot of excitement," Downs said of the home opener. "It's going to be joyful for me just to be on the field again, as always, and to be in the situation I've been put in. I'm just very thankful. To go out and play in front of a home crowd is going to be an awesome feeling."

Getting to watch him make plays in person like the strip-sack he had against the Giants will also be an awesome feeling for the Cowboys fans as well.

articles.title: “He put himself right there in the midst of danger”: Patrick Mahomes’ mental strength comes into play as he breaks records against Denver Broncos in Week 1
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ quarterback, impressed everyone as he got back to the field against the Denver Broncos after spending nine mo.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ quarterback, impressed everyone as he got back to the field against the Denver Broncos after spending nine months in recovery and training. Initially, there were many concerns about Patrick Mahomes’ injury but it seems he has bounced back from it.
