articles.title: B/R's Week 2 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: The first week of the 2026 NFL season is in the books. And for fantasy managers, it was a wild and wacky ride.
articles.body:
The first week of the 2026 NFL season is in the books. And for fantasy managers, it was a wild and wacky ride.

Some things went as expected—the highest-scoring running back of the first week was Baltimore's Derrick Henry, who has been known to have a big game every now and then. But the first wideout off draft boards on average was invisible, and the high scorer at the position went undrafted almost as often as he was.

Now, there are two types of fantasy managers—undefeated juggernauts and winless tomato cans. OK, that's not true, but the latter group feels that way. However, one of the keys to fantasy success is to not get too high or too low—especially early in the campaign. Complacency will get you cooked as quickly as freaking out.

Whether you're looking to stay on track or get your team back on it, Bleacher report has your back for Week 2. Tiered PPR Rankings? Check. Player commentary and advice? Check. The top-125 players overall for Week 2? Check.

So, let's, um, check out the Week 2 landscape.

Week 1 of the 2026 season went exactly how we suspected it would at the quarterback position in fantasy leagues.

It was no surprise to see Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills have a big week—even against a stout Houston Texans defense. But the rest of the top-five in fantasy points was filled with surprises.

Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars lit up the Cleveland Browns for four touchdown passes. Jaxson Dart of the New York Giants threw three scoring strikes and topped 50 rushing yards. Bryce Young of the Carolina Panthers had one of the best games of his professional career.

And Caleb Williams of the Chicago Bears? Williams threw for 269 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for two more on the way to the biggest fantasy score of the week under center.

It's important not to overreact to one game. But it was an…interesting start to the season nonetheless.

Allen and Josh Allen are elite fantasy options regardless of their opponent, and Allen faces a Detroit Lions defense that just surrendered over 400 passing yards to the New Orleans Saints. After watching the Bears drop 59 (!) points on the Panthers, Williams has moved into the top tier.

Fantasy managers rolling out a Tier 2 quarterback in Week 2 should feel pretty good about where they stand at the position. Patrick Mahomes didn't look like a guy who tore his ACL late last season against the Denver Broncos last week, and Dak Prescott and Jayden Daniels are both set up well in matchups against defenses that were first and second in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks a year ago.

The third tier of quarterbacks in Week 2 is a mixed bag of so-so starters. Dart looked great last week against Dallas, but he draws a far tougher matchup this week against an angry Rams team. Game script could mean a pedestrian day for Brock Purdy if the Niners get a big lead, while Matthew Stafford and Drake Maye are both trying to wash off the stink of a Week 1 clunker.

There's potential for some solid outings from the Tier 4 quarterbacks, but questions as well. Can Bryce Young come close to last week's numbers in what could be a lower-scoring matchup with the Falcons? Can Tyler Shough repeat last week's big game against the Lions, or was it a one-off? Can Bo Nix wash off the stink of his Week 1 dud against the Chiefs?

The fifth tier is a small one. It's also the end of the line for quarterbacks that can be started with even nominal confidence in fantasy leagues. The Dolphins offense looked abysmal last week, but rushing upside keeps Malik Willis on the fantasy fringes. Jacoby Brissett started off the 2026 season the same way he ended 2025—quietly posting low-end QB1 numbers.

Fantasy managers starting a Tier 6 quarterback are either playing in superflex leagues or already have serious issues under center. Only one quarterback in the tier finished last week inside the top-20 (Deshaun Watson), and that was due to a long touchdown pass in garbage time.

It was a big week for offenses across the NFL in Week 1. Teams averaged 24.7 points per game—the most in the opening weekend of the regular season since the AFL-NFL merger. Plenty of running backs got in on the fun—six topped 30 PPR points.

The most impressive outing of the week may well have been the last.

Kenneth Walker III wasn't the highest-scoring back of Week 1—that honor went to Derrick Henry (stunner). But Walker piled up 191 total yards (including 173 rushing) and found the end zone three times in his Chiefs debut.

One game does not a season make. But it was still exactly what fantasy managers were hoping for from Walker in his new home.

The Tier 1 running backs are all elite fantasy options and every week must-starts. Most came out of the gate strong in Week 1. The one who didn't is Christian McCaffrey, who actually had fewer carries than Kaelon Black in Australia. However, McCaffrey was reportedly dealing with cramps in a game the Niners controlled from the jump—no need to panic just yet.

The front of Tier 2 contains a pair of AFC West backs who went off last week in Walker and Ashton Jeanty—both could jump into the top tier with another big outing in Week 2. There are some questions at the back of the tier though—Chase Brown draws a tough matchup with the Texans this week, while Omarion Hampton rushed for under 45 yards in the opener against Arizona.

The third tier features multiple veterans coming off solid openers. Javonte Williams and David Montgomery didn't post big yardage numbers in Week 1, but multiple touchdowns propelled them into the top-10 in PPR points. D'Andre Swift got in on the offensive explosion by the Bears with three scores last week, but this week's matchup with Minnesota is considerably less favorable.

This small tier features backs with upside and uncertainty in equal measure. Chuba Hubbard was the Panthers' clear lead back in Week 1, but many still expect Jonathon Brooks to supplant him. Quinshon Judkins had a miserable Week 1 against the Jaguars' No. 1 run defense from a year ago. Travis Etienne didn't see the workload most expected a week ago—just nine carries against the Lions.

By the time you hit the fifth tier of running backs, things start getting dicey. If Week 1 was any indication, Tony Pollard is going to have a low fantasy ceiling in an abysmal Titans offense. The Denver duo of JK Dobbins and R.J. Harvey faces a Jacksonville defense that barely allowed 85 yards per game on the ground a year ago. Kyle Monangai had a big Week 1, but his touches could vary wildly from week to week.

We're in "maybe" flex territory now. Even if TreVeyon Henderson plays in Week 2, his touches could be limited as he recovers from an ankle injury. Jonathon Brooks needed a 48-yard catch to salvage even a "meh" 2026 debut for the Panthers. Blake Corum, Tyler Allgeier and Kaelon Black could all see 15 carries in Week 2—or five.

Tier 7 is deep league flexes and desperation plays. Maybe one of these backup backs will find the end zone or pick up some stats in garbage time. But there isn't a back in the tier who can be slotted in starting lineups without needing a double shot of Mylanta first.

There were any number of big-name wide receivers who started strong in Week 1—Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seahawks and Amon-Ra St. Brown of the Lions were both top-10 PPR options.

But the No. 1 wide receiver for the week was someone no one saw coming.

Granted, there was some buzz surrounding Jalen Coker of the Panthers as a late-round breakout candidate over the summer. But even Coker's own mother didn't expect the third-year pro to blow up against Chicago to the tune of eight catches for 138 yards and a pair of scores.

It was a week-winning stat line—that was probably wasted on benches in more fantasy leagues than not.

There's not a lot to say about the Tier 1 wide receivers other than if you have one, he's in the starting lineup. Ja'Marr Chase is a candidate for a "squeaky wheel" game after just two catches for 12 yards in Week 1, while Justin Jefferson will look to build on a strong start to the season despite an injury under center in the Twin Cities.

The Tier 2 wideouts aren't quite the mortal locks that the receivers above them are, but they are still rock-solid fantasy starts in Week 2. Rashee Rice of the Chiefs salvaged his first game with a touchdown, while CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens should rebound from a pedestrian Week 1 against a Commanders team that allowed the fifth-most PPR points per game to wideouts in 2025.

The wide receivers in Tier 3 are better suited to the WR2 slot on fantasy rosters than the top spot, but there are multiple players with top-10 upside. Christian Watson had a massive game in Green Bay's Week 1 loss to Minnesota, while Mike Evans and Brock Purdy appear to already have a strong rapport in San Francisco.

Tier 4 is comprised largely of wide receivers with considerable upside who are trying to shake off a down Week 1. Jaylen Waddle's Broncos debut was a mess—just one catch for two yards. While Coker was going nuts, Tetairoa McMillan finished Week 1 outside the top-30 receivers. Zay Flowers had a bonkers first half against the Colts, but he's questionable for Week 2 after aggravating a hamstring injury he suffered in camp.

Many are probably surprised to see Coker this low after his ridonkulous Week 1 stat line. But fantasy managers shouldn't overreact to one huge game any more than a bad one. With that said, Marvin Harrison Jr. had five fewer targets in the opener than Kendrick Bourne and caught just one pass. If he doesn't rebound this week, Harrison will be hard to start moving forward.

Welcome to the land of "You might have to start one of these wideouts, but you don't have to like it" section of this week's program. Carnell Tate is going to have trouble ever getting untracked if Tennessee's offense can't get going. Brian Thomas Jr. has clearly taken a back seat to Parker Washington (and possibly even Jakobi Meyers) in Jacksonville. Romeo Doubs is the new No. 1 wideout in New England with A.J. Brown out, but his Pats debut was a disaster.

There's a least some fantasy upside this far down the list in surprise standouts like Devaughn Vele and Caleb Douglas, both of whom posted at least WR2 numbers in Week 1. But while there's some upside in Tier 7, there is also an abundance of players with low fantasy floors—fantasy managers could be left holding the bag as easily as raking it in in Week 2 with this bunch.

These wide receivers are the bottom of the barrel—high-variance options who should be started only in the deepest of leagues. Denzel Boston is an excellent example—he was a top-25 wideout last week, but almost all of his production came on one play. Tread lightly—or just steer clear altogether.

OK, so things didn't quite go according to plan for fantasy managers who rolled out Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland in Week 1.

Loveland was a trendy breakout pick this year after a strong finish to his rookie year, with more than a few pundits speculating that he could crack the top tier at his position in 2026. Given that the Bears scored 59 points and amassed over 550 yards of offense against the Carolina Panthers, one would assume that Loveland's breakout had already started.

You know what they say bout assumptions—Loveland was targeted just twice in the game and didn't record a catch.

Loveland's goose-egg is a tough pill to swallow, and this week's visit from the Minnesota Vikings isn't favorable from a fantasy perspective.

But there's nothing to do but roll him out. The turnaround will come.

With Brock Bowers out with a knee injury, Trey McBride is a tier unto himself—only Isaiah Likely of the Giants had more PPR points among tight ends last week than McBride.

Not a lot has changed at tight end in one week—after McBride comes the three-man tier of Loveland, Tyler Warren and Tucker Kraft. None had an especially great game in Week 1, but in accordance with this week's theme all three deserve some patience. Of the trio, Kraft has the best fantasy matchup this week against the Jets.

Likely wasn't the only Tier 3 tight end who blew up in his first game of the season—Dallas Goedert found the end zone twice in the Eagles' nailbiter against the Washington Commanders, and Dalton Kincaid had five catches for 130 yards against the Houston Texans. So long as your starter is in one of the top-three tiers, you should be fine in Week 2.

Loveland wasn't the only big name at tight end who posted a big fat zero in Week 1—with third-string quarterback Cooper Rush under center for the Atlanta Falcons, Kyle Pitts was held catchless as well. Harold Fannin didn't fare much better—three targets, two catches and 21 yards against the Jaguars. Fannin is the better bet to rebound in Week 2—the Tampa Bay Buccaneers surrendered the fourth-most PPR points to tight ends last season.

The fifth tier of tight ends produced multiple viable fantasy starters last week—Mike Gesicki caught five passes for 78 yards and a score against Tampa, while Evan Engram was the lone bright spot for the Denver offense on Monday night. However, it's entirely possible we just saw the best game either tight end will have this season—don't get caught chasing big outings that are unlikely to be duplicated.

Fantasy managers with any other options should avoid the players in this tier—most have a low fantasy ceiling and an even lower floor. Brock Bowers is included here only because the Raiders continue to insist he could return in Week 2. I continue to insist that I will win the Powerball. Both are equally likely—or not.

There's a flip side to the record-setting offensive outburst we saw in Week 1. Quiet a few defenses took it on the chin—including a couple of elite units.

It's still too early to panic about the Houston Texans. It was a bit unsettling to see the ease with which the Buffalo Bills moved the ball in Week 1, but it's still the Bills—Buffalo allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing defenses in 2025. This week's matchup with the Bengals isn't great, but Houston should have more success rushing the passer in Week 2.

However, there's cause for genuine concern with the Denver Broncos. It's not just that the Broncos were boatraced in Kansas City. It's how they lost. The defense just looked bad. The tackling looked like a junior high team.

And in Week 2, the Broncos host a Jacksonville Jaguars team that was a buzzsaw offensively in Week 1 against the Browns.

The top tier of defenses this week is as much about the matchups as the defenses themselves. The Seahawks face a Cardinals team that gave up the seventh-most fantasy points to defenses last season. The Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans were both top-five fantasy matchups in 2025, and both teams looked terrible offensively in their 2026 openers.

Tier 2 is a combo platter of matchup plays, high-end defenses with OK (but not great) matchups and big names looking to bounce back. The Saints moved the ball all over the place last week but also gave up multiple big plays, so the Ravens should be a solid play. The Rams are far better defensively than what they showed in Week 1, and so are their SoFi Stadium roomies in the Chargers. Both defenses should rebound this week.

By the end of Tier 3, the defenses that can be started with a reasonable amount of confidence are just about exhausted. Given how badly the Broncos struggled offensively in Week 1, the Jaguars have gone from Week 1 rental to potential multi-week starter. If the Chiefs can contain Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, the team could post a second straight top-10 fantasy finish to open the season.

There's at least a little "Hail Mary" appeal with a couple of the Tier 4 defenses—the Dallas Cowboys and Chicago Bears face opponents in Week 2 who were kind to opposing defenses in 2025. But these are either bad defenses or OK units with sketchy matchups. Look elsewhere if at all possible.

Let's see, how best to put this? Don't do it. Sure, one of these defenses could log a pick-six or return a punt and pull a good fantasy outing out of the ether. But it's far more likely that fantasy managers will get little to nothing out of this batch of porous defensive units.

Generally speaking, a short leash is advisable with kickers. If a guy isn't scoring points, off to the waiver wire he goes—period. It doesn't matter who it is.

However, since I'm such a nice guy, we'll give Brandon Aubrey of the Dallas Cowboys one more chance.

Aubrey has one of the biggest legs in the game. Last year, only Jason Myers of the Seahawks had more points among kickers than Aubrey. But his Week 1 stat line was a major letdown. Zero field goal tries. A missed extra point. And two fantasy points.

The Cowboys should have more luck offensively this week against a Commanders team that was mediocre at best defensively a year ago. Provided that's the course, Aubrey's a good bet to turn things around.

However, if he has another down game, don't be afraid to cut bait.

Aubrey and Cam Little are in a class of their own among kickers. Both play on teams capable of piling up points and marching up and down the field. Both also have the ability to hit field goals from 60-plus yards without breaking a sweat.

The Tier 2 kickers are reliable weekly starters far more often than not—proven veteran options on good offenses with a track record of producing. Cameron Dicker is another big-name at the position who had a bad Week 1, but the Chargers should be able to get the offense back on track at home against the Raiders.

There's some appeal from a few of the Tier 3 kickers—most of whom are available on the waiver wire. Trey Smack is a big-legged youngster who nailed a 59-yarder last week. Chris Boswell isn't exciting, but he's been a consistent fantasy option for years. Jake Elliott and Tyler Bass both play for teams that should have offensive success this week.

Said it last week. Will say it next week. And the week after that. In 99 percent of fantasy leagues, if you're starting a kicker from the bottom tier at the position, something has gone terribly, terribly wrong.

Before we get to this week's list of the top-125 players overall, a couple of notes.

As always, the first is that there are no quarterbacks on this list. So, while it can help you make "flex" lineup decisions, in "superflex" leagues you need to ask yourself one question—is my QB2 any good? If he is, start him.

The second note is this. No one wants to start the season 0-1. But half of every league does it every year. Don't exacerbate the situation by panic-dropping players or making cute lineup calls two weeks into the season.

This isn't to say that hot (and cold) starts should be ignored. All information has value. But it's one week. Stars who started slow will turn things around—possibly as soon as this week. Week 1's surprise studs can just as easily be Week 2's duds that aren't a surprise at all.

Take a breath. Stay the course. Start your starters.

Every little thing is gonna be all right.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: Best Fits for Top Available NFL Free Agents After Week 1 Injuries
articles.summary: Injuries are part and parcel of playing professional football. While no one will get through the 2026 NFL season 100 percent healthy, some players had the misfortune to not even make it past Week 1 without picking up a significant ailment.
articles.body:
Injuries are part and parcel of playing professional football. While no one will get through the 2026 NFL season 100 percent healthy, some players had the misfortune to not even make it past Week 1 without picking up a significant ailment.

Although there weren't many major season-ending injuries suffered during the long stretch between Wednesday's NFL Kickoff Game and the Monday Night Football matchup that bookended the 16-game slate, plenty of injuries occured that are likely to keep some of the league's most notable players out for at least one game.

Teams are now scrambling to unearth replacements for their banged-up players before Week 2 gets underway. With time at a premium, it's imperative that these clubs make the most of their free-agent pickups and bring in players who mesh well with their roster and schemes.

With that in mind, here's a look at the best fits for some of the top available players still lingering in free agency.

The Seattle Seahawks began their tenure as reigning champions by gritting out a victory over the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch, but now must go without starting quarterback for a stretch after Sam Darnold suffered a " very unique soft-tissue injury " in the glute area.

Although it remains to be seen how long Darnold will be sidelined for—the team called it a "short-term" issue—Seattle will want to be proactive and bring in another quarterback as insurance for backup Drew Lock.

Given their aspirations of joining the Patriots and Kansas City Chiefs as the only back-to-back champs of the 21st century, the Seahawks should prioritize acquiring a proven player over a raw young passer. Josh Johnson, a grizzled 19-year veteran, fits the bill perfectly. Although he's currently on the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad, the Seahawks could pluck him off and add him to the active roster as their QB3.

Johnson offers an extensive amount of experience stemming from his time playing for 14 different teams since entering the league as fifth-round pick in the 2008 draft. He linked up with the Washington Commanders last season and did well in his first action since the 2021 campaign, going 1-1 across two starts while completing 63 percent of his throws for 372 yards and a touchdown on the year. Johnson also added 55 yards and a score on 12 totes.

Although Johnson wouldn't be pressed into action unless Lock goes down and second-year developmental project Jalen Milroe is either injured or ineffective after taking the reins, he's the type of steady old hand the Seahawks can trust if things go from bad to worse over these next few weeks.

The Cleveland Browns stumbled out of the gate, opening their season with a disheartening 34-10 defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars. To make matters worse, the team also lost backup running back Dylan Sampson to a severe knee injury, one that may potentially sideline him for the rest of the 2026 NFL season .

Cleveland couldn't get anything going on the ground against the Jags, with starter Quinshon Judkins getting held to 33 yards on 12 carries. Special teamer Raheim Sanders only gained a single yard on his lone tote, while rookie wideout KC Concepion wound up being the team's most efficient hand-off option after tallying 15 yards on three rushes.

Given the dismal state of the team's ground attack and Sampson's projected extensive absence, the Browns must make a move to reinforce the backfield as soon as possible. This could lead to a reunion with former starter Jerome Ford, who remains available after he failed to land with a team this offseason.

Ford was selected by Cleveland in the fifth round of the 2022 draft and found the most success in 2023 after taking over for an injured Nick Chubb. Ford finished his sophomore campaign with 1,132 yards and nine touchdowns from scrimmage. The back lost his starting role upon Chubb's return in 2024 and was relegated to third-string duties after the team drafted both Judkins and Sampson in 2025.

Although he caught on with the Washington Commanders at the start of the offseason, Ford was eventually released with an injury settlement ahead of cutdown day. Despite the discouraging cut, Ford could rejuvenate his career by returning to a club that needs him far more now than it did at this time last year.

Ford averaged a steady 4.3 yards per carry during his first stint in Cleveland and showed he can effectively contribute as both a rusher and receiver out of the backfield. If he can pass a physical, the Browns shouldn't hesitate to sign him as Judkins' backup.

The Baltimore Ravens opened their 2026 campaign with a big 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts. While the team loudly stated its case to be considered a legitimate Super Bowl contender, it also took a hit when both star wideout Zay Flowers and promising rookie Ja'Kobi Lane were injured in the contest.

According to ESPN's Jamison Hensley , Lane reportedly fractured his wrist and could be out an extended stretch. The Flowers injury isn't as serious but potentially even more concerning, as he had piled up 150 yards and a touchdown on an economical five catches before going down with a hamstring issue in the first half. While the initial prognosis is good, Flowers has been dealing with hamstring problems throughout the offseason and may need some time off to avoid risking the injury getting worse.

With the inconsistent Rashod Bateman, special teamer LaJohntay Wester and recent practice squad call-up Chris Moore being the only active wideouts to make it through Week 1 unscathed, Baltimore must bring in a proven veteran like Tyreek Hill to reinforce the position.

Hill's blazing speed, elite athleticism and strong hands would help him play a role in Baltimore's passing attack from the jump, potentially even seamlessly transitioning into Flowers' high-volume role if called upon.

Hill hasn't seen the field since suffering a devastating knee injury in Week 4 of last season, but is nearly ready to return after an extensive rehabilitation period. Drew Rosenhaus, Hill's longtime agent, appeared on the Pat McAfee Show last week and revealed that his client should be "100 percent good to go" at some point within the next month (h/t Pro Football Talk's Josh Alper ).

Considering the injuries this already-thin receiving corps has been dealing with, adding Hill as soon as he's ready to play again should be atop the Baltimore front office's to-do list.

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

The Washington Commanders kept things close in their 24-22 defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles, but that outcome could have been different had Chig Okonkwo not suffered a hamstring injury that knocked him out of the game in the third quarter.

If Okonkwo is out for a stretch—and hamstring injuries are notoriously tricky—Washington will be forced to ask John Bates to fill void and promote Ben Sinnott into a backup role. Unfortunately for the Commanders, neither player is a serious receiving threat, with each lacking the unique combination of size, speed and hands that Okonkwo brings to the table.

Rather than enter a pivotal Week 2 clash against the Dallas Cowboys with an underwhelming tight end situation, it would behoove the Commanders to reunite with former starter Zach Ertz. Although the 13-year veteran remains unsigned, he could still provide a major boost to this offense without needing much time to get brought up to speed.

Ertz is already familiar with quarterback Jayden Daniels and much of the Washington roster after spending the past two seasons serving as one of the team's top weapons. Ertz particularly thrived in 2024 when he racked up 654 yards and seven touchdowns on 66 catches. While he injuries prompted a regression last year, Ertz still posted a solid 50/504/4 line in the 13 games he was available for.

Although he doesn't have much tread left on his tires at the age of 35, Ertz still profiles as a far better Okonkwo replacement than any of the current members of Washington's roster. He may not be the fastest player at the position, but an elite football IQ, good hands and a strong rapport with Daniels more than makes up for that fading athleticism.

The Dallas Cowboys not only suffered a tough 28-20 defeat to the rival New York Giants to open the 2026 NFL season, but lost some key members of their defense for a stretch in the process. With safety Malik Hooker and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown both set to miss several games , the team desperately needs to bring in quality reinforcements.

One of the shrewdest moves Dallas could make at this juncture is adding Bobby Wagner. The 14-year veteran remains unsigned despite a history of success throughout his Hall of Fame-worthy career and could provide an immediate boost to this defense.

Wagner may be in the twilight of his career, but he proved he's still an asset during his time with the Washington Commanders last year. He appeared in all 17 games for the club—marking the fourth consecutive season he didn't miss a single contest—and recorded 162 tackles and a pair of interceptions. He's only a season removed from making the most recent of his 10 Pro Bowl appearances and would be the league's active leading tackler by a wide margin with 2,000 when he signs.

With his unparalleled instincts and experience, Wagner could come in and instantly make a difference for the Cowboys. He may lack sideline-to-sideline speed at the age of 36, but his ability to diagnose plays and attack the football gives him an edge over any other linebacker currently available on the free-agent market.

Coming to terms with Wagner would help the Cowboys weather the storm of defensive injuries they are currently dealing with. Once Overshown is ready to return, Wagner can slide into a rotational backup role and contribute situationally while also serving as a leader for the team both on and off the field. It's a perfect fit for both sides and would help Dallas get back on track after a rough start to the season.

articles.title: Jaxson Dart's girlfriend Marissa Ayers shines in Week 1 win, a Giants-Cowboys fan fight & Ole Miss tension
articles.summary: Wednesday Screencaps spotlights Marissa Ayers, the sorority girl turned Jaxson Dart girlfriend, after her viral TikTok Week 1 recap video drop.
articles.body: Good morning everyone and welcome to Wednesday Screencaps in the middle of September. This isn't just another Wednesday. It's the last one for the summer of 2026. Next week at this time, your wife will be on the couch at 8 p.m. with her comfy blanket proclaiming, "It's chilly in here tonight." I know, I know, I know...you live in the South and it's 110 degrees with the humidity right now. I don't care. There's something in female DNA that tells women to proclaim a chill in the air the minute it turns to fall. There will also be alarm bells going off in their heads that it's time to pick apples. Guys, prepare yourself. Moving along ... I spent the preseason pleading with you guys to keep an eye on the Giants O/U win total of 7.5. I also said all eyes needed to be on Marissa Ayers, the sorority girl turned girlfriend of Jaxson Dart, who, I predicted would become the face of NFL wives and girlfriends. Move over Madison Beer. JAXSON DART TAKES BRUTAL HIT EARLY IN GIANTS VS COWBOYS OPENER BUT WHAT HAPPENED NEXT WAS KIND OF SURPRISING How about the Week 1 performance out of both of these future superstars? The Giants are up a game in the division after beating the Cowboys and now have a 58% probability of making the playoffs. Then there's the performance turned in by Ayers. "Only the beginning," she declared Tuesday on TikTok while releasing her Week 1 recap video. Guys, it's time to get on the bandwagon. I hope you're holding those OVER 7.5 win tickets. The Giants have the 26th hardest remaining schedule, including games against the Cardinals, Browns, Titans and Colts. articles.title: Cleveland Browns Stock Up, Stock Down Entering Week 2 of the 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: No team looked worse in the NFL in Week 1 than the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
No team looked worse in the NFL in Week 1 than the Cleveland Browns.

Todd Monken's coaching debut was marked by undisciplined offense and sloppy defense as the Jaguars ran up a 34-10 lead. The point differential was the worst in the league on opening weekend.

There wasn't much that went right. The Jaguars figure to be one of the top teams in the AFC this season, but the lack of competitiveness certainly stung.

The reality is that this is a season where individual performances will need to be evaluated. Every week there will be players who make their case to be part of the long-term picture.

There will also be those who play themselves into a demotion. Let's take a look at both categories heading into this week's road trip to Tampa Bay.

It would have been nice to see Denzel Boston make plays earlier in the game. But he didn't see his first target until there was eight seconds left in the second quarter.

He saw three in the second half and he made them count. His first catch moved the chains on a 2nd-and-13 before he made the best play of the afternoon with a 46 yard reception for a touchdown. He clearly established himself as the team's best deep threat moving forward.

Austin Barber got the opportunity to show he can be a starter due to Teven Jenkins being out with an injury. He made the most of it.

The Browns struggled to protect Deshaun Watson or make a ton of running lanes, but Barber sported the team's best PFF grade and was ranked No. 1 among all rookie offensive linemen through Sunday.

That could make it difficult to bump him out of the starting lineup.

Raheim Sanders was another rookie who was pushed into a bigger role due to injury. Dylan Sampson's knee injury opened some opportunity for the rookie and he took advantage.

He was a reliable safety valve in the passing game with three receptions for 25 yards. His 74 yard kickoff return was one of the few highlights of the game as well. He should serve nicely as the team's second running back while Sampson recovers.

Todd Monken can say all he wants about the good things he saw on film and his faith in Deshaun Watson. The quarterback was miserable on Sunday and was a driving force behind the blowout loss.

Watson's stat line was deceiving by the end of the afternoon, but his play early in the game was disastrous. The offensive line might not have played well, but he contributed to his own pressures with deep drops in the pocket.

He took five sacks, threw a momentum-killing pick on the first drive of the game and missed open receivers all afternoon. If he puts up a similar performance against Tampa, the pleas for Shedeur Sanders will only grow louder.

Zion Johnson is supposed to be a key cog in the Browns rebuilt offensive line. He was far from it on Sunday.

Johnson showed why the Chargers were alright with letting him walk in free agency this offseason. He had two holding penalties on the same drive to end the second quarter.

He also appeared to miss an assignment that brought immediate pressure on Watson when he threw his first pick. It was a sloppy debut from a guard who needs to offer consistency and more help in the run game.

Deshaun Watson caught a lot of the blame for the Browns 10-point performance on Sunday. Second-year running back Quinshon Judkins probably deserves more than he's getting. He finished the day with 12 carries for 33 yards (2.8 ypc).

The initial reaction might be to blame the offensive line, but ESPN Analytics credited the Browns with the seventh-highest run block win rate in the league. Next Gen Stats noted that Judkins had the second-lowest yards over expected per attempt while facing no eight-man boxes the whole game.

In other words, the Browns had no shot at leaning on their running game while the quarterback was struggling. Judkins was not explosive and seemed to get less than what the offensive line blocked for him.

There wasn't much good to parse from the defensive performance, but Mason Graham is one of the few exceptions. The second-year defensive tackle looked more explosive than last season and gave them something to build around.

He already topped his sack total from last season, taking down Trevor Lawrence on a 3rd-and-1 to get the defense off the field.

He also chipped in another two tackles for a loss. A disruptive interior pressure player can be a game-changer and Graham flashed that potential in this game.

It was unclear what second-round pick Emmanuel McNeil-Warren's role would be on the defense. The Toledo product ended up being the third safety and lined up deep, in the box and as a slot corner in at least one of his 14 snaps in the game.

McNeil-Warren wasn't stellar by any means, but he was quick to fill the alley in the run game and made a good open-field tackle on Bhaysul Tuten.

At the very least, the rookie showed he could continue to be deployed in that role. At best, he should be considered as a replacement for Ronnie Hickman if the veteran doesn't look better soon.

We'll start the Stock Down section the same way Trevor Lawrence spend much of his Sunday afternoon: Picking on Myles Harden.

According to PFF , Harden gave up a perfect 158.3 passer rating when targeted on Sunday. The Jaguars clearly had a gameplan to find Harden and work the slot. Parker Washington led the team with six targets, catching five of them for 83 yards and a touchdown.

Harden was a weak link on paper heading into the season. He didn't do anything in Week 1 to shake that perception.

It's not fair to compare Jared Verse to Myles Garrett. There's a reason the Browns got massive draft compensation in addition to Verse.

But can we at least compare him to an average starting NFL defensive end?

Verse struggled mightily in his first game as the team's top pass-rusher. Additional attention in the form of chips and double teams were too much for Verse to handle. He didn't register a single pressure on a day where the Browns hardly blitzed and needed to disrupt Lawrence.

Verse has work to do to live up his potential as the team's top edge player.

The Browns have a lot of young pieces on defense so it was key to bring in a veteran like Quincy Williams to provide consistency and leadership. Unfortunately, Williams was consistently uninvolved in the defense in his debut.

He played every defensive snap of the game, but managed to only be a part of four tackles.

The most notable thing he did was become a meme for spending the first few seconds of a play in coverage frozen in one spot. Lawrence threw a ball over his head for a big gain to get inside the 30 on the play.

He has to be better to play out his two-year contract in Cleveland.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills Stock Up, Stock Down Entering Week 2 of the 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The moment is nearly here. After more than half a century at "The Ralph," the Buffalo Bills will christen their new home Thursday night against the Detroit Lions.
articles.body:
The moment is nearly here. After more than half a century at "The Ralph," the Buffalo Bills will christen their new home Thursday night against the Detroit Lions.

They're carrying plenty of momentum into the historic occasion after edging the Houston Texans in a 36-31 Week 1 thriller. That wild shootout featured unforgettable performances from key playmakers, but it also exposed some alarming flaws on both sides of the ball.

As a result, there are quite a few extremes to explore in our Bills stock report entering Week 2.

It's hard to believe the MVP favorite's stock could be higher than it was entering the season, but it had to grow at least a little as Allen willed the Buffalo offense to life in his first game as a 30-year-old.

In a heroic performance, Allen posted a 140.0 passer rating on throws that traveled at least 15 yards and was 6-for-8 for 111 yards on third down. He generated a combined four passing and rushing touchdowns, turning the ball over zero times and absorbing just two sacks against one of the best defenses in the NFL.

Last year's leading rusher looked like he was picking up where he left off when he ran for 20 yards on his first two carries, but Cook compiled just 26 rushing yards on nine attempts over the course of the next three and a half quarters.

He salvaged the performance to an extent with a big 12-yard gain with Buffalo backed up late in the game, but even that carry resulted in a fumble that might have cost the Bills the victory had O'Cyrus Torrence not jumped on it.

Again, the Bills were up against an elite defense in a challenging road environment. And the offensive line was not crisp (more on that unit in a moment). Cook has also earned the benefit of the doubt, but the pressure is on against Detroit.

Against said stellar defense, Moore made an immediate impact as the new No. 1 receiver in Buffalo.

The 29-year-old veteran caught five passes for 100 yards and a touchdown while drawing a huge defensive pass interference penalty to set up another score and attracting double teams that opened up the rest of the field for fellow pass-catchers to go to work.

It was one of the top dozen or so games of Moore's career, which is saying a lot considering that he came into the league in 2018.

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

Coleman was on the field for 29 snaps but made a clear positive impact on just one play—a catch and lateral that went into the books as a one-yard reception. He was also the intended receiver on a failed two-point conversion attempt late in the fourth quarter.

It was the third-least productive game of his career.

That said, have we mentioned this was a tricky opponent? When you're not a regular starter, these types of outings sometimes happen. Let's give Coleman some time.

But what really hurts Coleman's stock is the fact Palmer was targeted twice and scored a huge touchdown despite playing far fewer snaps than his third-year teammate against the Texans.

The 26-year-old Canadian was held without a touchdown in 2025, but he actually started strong as well before injuries marred much of his first campaign with the Bills. If he can stay healthy this time around, Palmer could outperform Coleman and become a consistent producer for the first time since his early seasons with the Chargers.

On several occasions in Houston, this veteran unit looked unprepared and disorganized. On some of those occasions, it appeared guys were schemed into disadvantageous positions.

But even beyond that, nobody had a great day.

Left tackle Dion Dawkins whiffed on a critical fourth-down block and lost several battles on the edge, new left guard Alec Anderson was overmatched often, center Connor McGovern had a sloppy performance, right guard O'Cyrus Torrence was PFF's seventh-lowest-rated qualified guard, and right tackle Spencer Brown put his quarterback in a really bad spot on a critical second-half third-down play.

It's a miracle they gave up just two sacks, although they were penalized four times.

This group is not young, and it lost some continuity with the departure of David Edwards. The competition was fierce on Sunday, but it's fair to be somewhat concerned about this line entering another tough spot against Detroit.

As in, few players in the league saw their stock climb like Kincaid in Week 1.

In the best game of his career to date, the former first-round pick caught three 35-plus-yard passes in a span of 30 minutes in Houston. Prior to that 30-minute window, he had made just two 35-yard grabs in his entire career!

In fact, no tight end in the league had more 35-yard receptions in the entirety of the 2025 season than Kincaid had in a span of seven drives against the Texans.

For all intents and purposes, Chubb is being paid $853,000 per game.

In his debut game for the Bills, the two-time Pro Bowler missed at least a pair of tackles and didn't come particularly close to a sack while generating just a few pressures all afternoon.

Considering the damage Greg Rousseau was doing on the other side against a mediocre offensive line and an oft-confused quarterback, that's a far-from-ideal start for Chubb.

Buffalo's Week 1 victory in Houston was essentially bookended by strip sacks from Rousseau, who in addition to those plays registered three hits on Stroud and shined when dropping into coverage.

It was one of the top three performances of his career to date, and a strong sign that the 26-year-old will flourish and become an elite defender in Jim Leonhard's system.

Yikes. We knew this might have been a soft spot headed into the season, but the three-man cornerback crew of Christian Benford, Maxwell Hairston and Dee Alford did very little to inspire confidence in the opener.

Benford was beaten routinely throughout the game, ultimately giving up eight catches for 85 yards, according to PFF . He and Hairston missed a combined four tackles, while Hairston and Alford got their signals crossed on a blown coverage that nearly cost the Bills the game.

Alford signed a three-year, $15.8 million contract to join the Bills in the offseason, but the 28-year-old vet looked lost for much of his debut in support of two overmatched boundary starters.

Unfortunately, that group will have its hands full again with Detroit's stacked pass-catching corps on Thursday night.

Two momentous tackles for loss and a sack highlighted one of the finest performances of Walker's young career, as the sophomore fourth-round pick gave us a strong indication that his promising rookie season was not a fluke.

The massive 22-year-old nose tackle has an extremely bright future, and it's easy to envision him showing the progress he's made to a national audience with a stellar performance Thursday night against Detroit.

Defensive Coordinator Jim Leonhard: DOWN

On far too many occasions during Leonhard's debut in this role, his personnel appeared to be confused. That unit attacked as expected, but not a lot got home beyond a few key sacks from Rousseau and Walker, leaving the secondary vulnerable while the off-ball linebackers scrambled to keep up with lost leverage.

The Bills were crushed in the time-of-possession battle as the defense once again failed to get off the field on third down, continuing a trend that the team hoped would die out with the conclusion of the Sean McDermott era.

This is Leonhard's first time running an NFL defense, so it would be unfair to condemn the hire one week in. That said, it was a discouraging start that saw a relatively talented unit give up 31 points to C.J. Stroud's offense. And if not for some hero plays by a few standout players, it might have been a lot worse.

Let's see what adjustments Leonhard makes and how much his guys can cut down on communication errors against the unforgiving Lions in Week 2.

In the 2023 playoffs, Bass missed a game-tying 44-yard field goal attempt as the Bills fell to the Chiefs by three points. In 2024, he missed four attempts between 40 and 49 yards as well as five extra points. In 2025, he missed the entire season due to a hip/groin injury.

With all of that in mind, a 6-for-6 season opener (three field goals, three extra points) including a 46-yarder to open the scoring on the season is quite encouraging.

articles.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter fires back at Bears ‘regression’ talk after 59-37 win
articles.summary: Caleb Williams accounted for four touchdowns.
articles.body:
ESPN's Adam Schefter pushed back strongly against concerns that the Chicago Bears could regress in the 2026 NFL season. Speaking on "The Adam Schefter Podcast," Schefter responded to Ty Schmit's question about Chicago's Week 1 performance with a blunt message.

"Regress my a–. I mean, give me a break," Schefter said.

The Bears opened the season with a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers . Chicago produced 552 total yards, including 291 rushing yards, while Caleb Williams accounted for four touchdowns.

Williams threw for 269 yards and two touchdowns while adding 65 rushing yards. D'Andre Swift rushed for 124 yards and three touchdowns, while rookie Kyle Monangai added 100 rushing yards.

Schefter pointed toward head coach Ben Johnson's approach as another reason for optimism. Johnson entered the season saying he wanted Chicago to become the NFL's highest-scoring offense.

"It's unbelievable, right? Like, what's incredible is that this is what Ben Johnson said," Schefter said, about the outside pressure surrounding his comments. "And when he said that he wanted to be the highest-scoring offense and set records, we all talked about the fact that he was just putting an even larger target on his back for the coming season."

Johnson's offense scored eight touchdowns and produced points in every quarter. The Bears also scored three straight touchdowns after Carolina tied the game 31-31 in the third quarter.

Bears offense gives Adam Schefter reason for confidence

Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) with Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) after the game at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Schefter pointed to Johnson's repeated ambition. "We want to be the best… want to set the records. We want to win Super Bowls," Johnson said after the game, according to Schefter. "And it's a different message than we get from other coaches."

He thinks Johnson understands how to connect with fans while maintaining demanding standards.

"He understands this is entertainment," Schefter said. "This is part of the deal. People love to turn to football for their escape. They want to be brought in. They want to be amused. And Ben Johnson is providing incredible coaching and great entertainment and fun for the fans that follow the Bears."

Chicago's offensive structure offered more than just a high-scoring total. The Bears ran effectively, protected Williams and created opportunities through multiple skill players.

Johnson also praised Williams' preparation before the game. " I could kind of tell Saturday night when we did our quarterback meeting one last time that he was just on top of it," he said.

However, the defense remains a concern after allowing 478 yards and 37 points. That issue could matter against stronger opponents. Still, Schefter sees enough from Chicago's offense to dismiss early regression concerns.

"Do you doubt that they're going to make a run for the points record after 59 in Week 1?" Schefter asked, pointing towards the 2013 Broncos' NFL single-season record of 606 points. They had an offense that averaged nearly 38 points per game.

Schmit agreed, even admitting his Packers connection made the praise difficult. "This guy is awesome," he said of Johnson.

articles.title: Bills QB Josh Allen achieves impressive scoring feat against Texans
articles.summary: Josh Allen has now scored 300 combined passing and rushing touchdowns faster than any player in NFL history.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills superstar quarterback Josh Allen added another feat to his career resume on Sunday during his team's 36-31 win against the Houston Texans , becoming the fastest quarterback in NFL history to reach 300 combined passing and rushing touchdowns .

Allen reached the milestone in his 129th career game. He continued a run of production that has made him one of the NFL's most difficult players to defend. Allen's total comes after years of effective play as the NFL's most dangerous dual-threat quarterback.

The achievement separates Allen from other prolific quarterbacks by highlighting the versatility of his game. He has delivered explosive plays through the air, extended drives with his legs and repeatedly finished possessions himself near the end zone throughout his career.

Allen's feat coming in a tough matchup against what may be the best defense in the NFL in the Texans' unit, adds more distinction to what he was able to accomplish. His performance again illustrated the combination of arm strength, mobility and physicality that has shaped the Bills ' offense in recent memory.

The 30-year-old Allen's scoring versatility has helped establish the Bills as a consistent Super Bowl contender in the league and remains central to the team's pursuit of postseason success.

Bills Wire will continue to provide updates throughout the 2026 NFL season.

articles.title: Titans Fan to Honor Chris Johnson With MetLife Stadium Walk After Being Called Out by Jets
articles.summary: A Tennessee Titans fan has agreed to walk from Nashville to New Jersey after watching their team concede a 23-10 season-opening loss to the New York Jets.
articles.body:
A Tennessee Titans fan has agreed to walk from Nashville to New Jersey after watching their team concede a 23-10 season-opening loss to the New York Jets.

The fan posted Tuesday on social media indicating they are going to follow through on their promise to attempt the 900-mile feat.

According to A to Z Sports' Austin Stanley , "the walk is going to happen, under one condition: this is now a fundraiser for ALS research in honor of Titans legend Chris Johnson."

Johnson announced in June he had been diagnosed with ALS at age 39.

The user previously wrote they would "walk from MetLife Stadium all the way to Nissan Stadium non stop" if the Titans lost in Week 1.

That post was followed the next day by a promise to donate $100 for every Jets point scored to a local charity.

The Jets followed up their victory by encouraging the fan to follow through on their original promise.

According to the fan, there will be "more details coming soon" about the walk. The Titans will meanwhile prepare for a Week 2 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles this Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Nashville.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 2: What do we make of the Rams without Myles Garrett?
articles.summary: The Rams remain in the top 5 but for how long? Meanwhile the Niners and Giants made the biggest jumps in the league. Headed in the opposite direction: the Co...
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

The Los Angeles Rams losing a weird game in Australia, for which they gambled that an aggressive travel plan wouldn't affect them but were obviously wrong, isn't that bad. They played terribly but it's fine to excuse it to having to play across the world.

But then, after not posting a single stat in a quiet Rams debut, Myles Garrett said his knee wasn't feeling well. A few days later, it was reported that Garrett was having knee surgery. On Monday, Rams head coach Sean McVay said there's no timetable for Garrett's return . He'll be out at least four weeks on injured reserve.

The Rams came into the season as the clear Super Bowl favorite , and that's already in question. It's not just losing Garrett, the best defensive player in the NFL. Matthew Stafford is 38 and he looked awful in the opener. When Rich Gannon won his first NFL MVP at age 37, like Stafford did last season, he threw only nine touchdowns the rest of his career. The age cliff finds everyone. Davante Adams , at 33, was a non-factor in the opener against the 49ers . The defense around Garrett didn't play well. Maybe it was all Australia. Maybe not.

Going forward without Garrett for however long is scary for this defense. The Rams had to trade Jared Verse to Cleveland in the Garrett deal, so they now have a big hole at defensive end. Aaron Donald being a force after returning from two years off is a lot more questionable without Garrett around to command double teams. The 49ers gained 379 yards and had no problems in the air or on the ground. Again, maybe that's just fatigue from a long trip, but we don't know yet. We also don't know if the long trip will impact the Rams for a few weeks to come. The Rams face the Giants on Monday night in Week 2, and that matchup doesn't look so easy after the Giants played well in their opening-game win against the Cowboys .

It's typically not a good idea to overreact to Week 1. The Raiders won at New England in last season's opener. Las Vegas went 3-14 and the Patriots went 14-3. Weird things happen in the beginning. However, there should be concern about the Rams. Not enough to send them way down the rankings, but enough that their standing as the clear Super Bowl favorite, or even the favorite in the NFC West, is in question. It's a top-heavy team and there are significant worries about their stars just one week into the season. We might not get a clear picture of who the Rams are until Garrett returns and shows he's back to his normal self. Whenever that will be.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 1 of the NFL season:

Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said success wouldn't be defined by wins or losses but development, and while he got a hard time for saying it, it's true for the 2026 Dolphins. In that way, it was good to see rookies like linebacker Jacob Rodriguez (a game-high 14 tackles and he played all 68 defensive snaps) and receiver Caleb Douglas (five catches, 94 yards) play well. This team still has a significantly insufficient roster, hence why it is in this spot even though it didn't embarrass itself like the …

An argument can be made that the Titans deserve to be No. 32. No team looked worse in Week 1. Against a Jets team that was 3-14 last season, the Titans had seven first downs and three points before their final possession, when they trailed by 20 points. Tennessee forced one punt and zero turnovers in the first three quarters. If you get dominated by the Jets at home, it could be a very long season. It probably explains the booing that fans gave the Titans. "When you lose, you're a loser," head coach Robert Saleh bluntly said afterward , acknowledging the discontent. Could more be on the immediate horizon? Up next for the Titans is a home game against the Eagles.

The Browns ' defense is supposed to keep them in games, even with Jared Verse replacing Myles Garrett. That wasn't the case in the opener as the Browns looked like they really missed Jim Schwartz as defensive coordinator. Trevor Lawrence had four touchdowns and Jacksonville had 31 points with 12:08 left in the third quarter. If Cleveland's defense is bad, there's no hope at a respectable season.

It's hard to get too excited about the start of the season when Cooper Rush is QB1. Head coach Kevin Stefanski gave no update Monday on who'll be the starter for Week 2 vs. the Panthers . Michael Penix Jr . might return soon, but will that fix much? Atlanta's defense played well in the Falcons' loss at Pittsburgh , but that probably has more to do with the Steelers ' offense that was held to 3-of-13 on third downs and 0-for-2 on fourth. Despite the quagmire everywhere around him, Bijan Robinson still managed 83 rushing yards and 90 receiving yards. So there, Falcons fans have one reason to be excited.

It shouldn't be a surprise that the Cardinals looked good on offense. Their quarterback situation isn't ideal but they have good skill position players. The surprise of their season-opening upset win was Arizona's defense. The Chargers got just 268 yards, they sacked Justin Herbert three times and had an interception and fumble recovery. Andrew Wingard , who had the interception of Herbert, had something he partially got off his chest postgame. "Everyone has been trashing this defense, trashing coach [Nick] Rallis," Wingard said of his defensive coordinator . "It's like … I'm going to be polite and not say what I want to say, but — it's not gratifying because it'd only be gratifying if you cared about it, but I'm just happy for all these guys." Arizona was eighth in EPA ( expected points added ) allowed per play through Sunday's Week 1 games. The Cardinals were projected to have one of the NFL's worst defenses this season, but that wasn't the case in the opener. A matchup against the Seahawks now looks more interesting.

We'll likely look back at the Jets' Week 1 win and realize the Titans really are that bad. However, allowing 195 yards to any NFL team is impressive. The Jets gained 367 yards and generally looked sharp in all ways on offense. Head coach Aaron Glenn needs to show improvement this season and he's off to a great start, even if it was against Tennessee.

The focus was on the Bears' offense , but the Panthers' defense was part of that story. Carolina had never allowed more than 52 points in a game before allowing 59 on Sunday. The Panthers spent big on the defense in the offseason and the results for Week 1 were awful. They wasted a fantastic performance by Bryce Young , who had 361 yards and three touchdowns passing and rushed for another score. Defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero might be on the hot seat early this season. "Like I said, it's embarrassing, but ultimately, I'm taking a really positive outlook from this because we can only get better from here," Panthers outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips said, via the team's site .

The Raiders can thank the schedule makers. Getting Miami at home to start the season was great for a team that had so many changes, including a new head coach in Klint Kubiak. They still had to execute no matter the opponent and the Raiders did just that, winning 27-13. It was without tight end Brock Bowers , who will hopefully be back soon from a meniscus trim in his knee. It was a good start, though the Raiders had a good start last season with a win at New England. This time they have to build on it.

Daniel Jones returning for Week 1, a little more than nine months after tearing his Achilles, always felt aggressive. And Jones didn't play well in Week 1. He was 28th among 30 qualified quarterbacks in adjusted EPA per play through Sunday's Week 1 games. Pair that with a defense that allowed 506 yards to the Ravens , and there should be plenty of concern in Indianapolis after just one game.

The Saints have a rightful complaint that a defensive touchdown was taken off the board due to a convoluted explanation of why Jared Goff 's pass that went backward was actually incomplete. With that play, the Saints probably win a game that they eventually lost in overtime. Still, being a 2-point conversion away from beating a talented Lions team on the road is a positive sign for the season.

Everything was labored with Jayden Daniels and the Commanders' offense . The line didn't protect well but Daniels often held the ball too long, perhaps because his receivers weren't getting open. He averaged 3.41 seconds per throw, the slowest among all QBs through Sunday's games, per Next Gen Stats. ( H/T to reporter Tashan Reed for pointing that out .) The Eagles have a good defense and that led to some of the issues. But the opener wasn't a good omen, especially for new coordinator David Blough . At least he has Daniels in his corner. The QB defended the shovel pass play that the Eagles stuffed on a 2-point conversion attempt, preventing a tie in the final minute of regulation. "It was the right call," Daniels told reporters postgame . "Anything Blough calls, man. I'm with him. Regardless, however everybody else might want to view it, man, I'm with Blough 100%."

The Buccaneers played well enough to win at the Bengals but they turned it over four times, one of which was returned for a touchdown and another that came at the Bengals' 4-yard line. You can't ignore that because it's a continuation of the sloppiness that cost the Bucs a division title last season. The good news for the Bucs is the division is still just as bad. Every NFC South team is 0-1.

The Steelers got a win but it wasn't pretty. Facing a Falcons team down to its third quarterback, the Steelers led by just three points in the fourth quarter before T.J. Watt had an interception return for a touchdown. Particularly troubling was the offense, which had the worst success rate in the NFL for Week 1. The run game really struggled, with 2.8 yards per carry. And that's against a Falcons defense that wasn't projected to be very good.

There's nothing good to say about the Chargers' Week 1 loss. It was so dispiriting that head coach Jim Harbaugh lamented sitting his starters for most of the preseason . The offense, with new coordinator Mike McDaniel, had two plays longer than 15 yards against an Arizona defense that isn't expected to be good. ( Don't tell Andrew Wingard I said that .) The defense, without last year's star coordinator Jesse Minter, allowed points or a missed field goal on seven of 10 possessions before a kneel-down at the end. The Chargers' early-season schedule is brutal , and the Cardinals game was supposed to be a rare easy win.

Nobody in Wisconsin wants to hear about how many yards Green Bay had or that the Packers outplayed the Vikings for most of the game. They want to know why the Packers, who lost five straight games last season, including multiple blown second-half leads, keep failing late in games. The Packers were outscored 22-0 in the fourth quarter. There has to be better answers for why the Packers are collapsing late. "It'll be a topic of conversation for all you guys until we do it," Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said . "That's the bottom line."

The Vikings won and that's a great way to start the season, but it's not like they played well. They were outgained 419-239. The Packers had 6.3 yards per play to just 3.9 for the Vikings. Minnesota won a game in which it lost Kyler Murray in the first quarter to a concussion, so squeezing out a victory is still a very good result but improvement needs to be made, and a lot of that will depend on Murray's status.

No team had a better EPA on offense than the Giants in Week 1 — which means no team had a worse EPA on defense than the Cowboys. Maybe team owner Jerry Jones was right to be "nervous" before kickoff Sunday night. Maybe everyone was too quick to assume that the Dallas' exhaustive defensive issues from a season ago were fixed. Despite new personnel and a new coordinator, the same communication issues that led to blown coverages showed up again in the loss to New York . Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones took a measured view of the wreckage, telling 105.3 The Fan (via The Athletic's Jon Machota ): "Felt really good and still do about our football team. We just probably had a little unrealistic expectations in terms of what we could do, especially on the defensive side of the ball with all the new faces and a brand new coordinator." Indeed, nobody should completely overreact to Week 1. But after a horrendous performance in the season opener, the Cowboys' defense now has to show evidence, starting Week 2 vs. the Commanders , it's any better than it was last season.

A lot will be made of coordinator Davis Webb taking over play-calling from Sean Payton and the Broncos ' offense looking terrible in his first game doing it. That's not all that was wrong with Denver. The defense was rock solid last season but was miserable Monday night against the Chiefs . There were numerous missed tackles as the Chiefs rushed for more than 200 yards. The Broncos were very unlikely to replicate a 14-win season, but there was good reason to believe they were still capable of winning the AFC West again. They'll have to play far better on both sides of the ball if they want to keep the division race competitive this season.

No team had a better offensive EPA per play through Sunday's Week 1 games than the Giants. Not even the Bears, who scored 59 points. What stood out was the impact new tight end Isaiah Likely had. He led the Giants with eight catches for 78 yards and two touchdowns. If the Giants' offense stays mostly healthy, perhaps this can be a surprise playoff team.

The defense should be fine when it's not facing Josh Allen . If that's the case, the positive about the loss to the Bills is that the offense looked good. Houston ranked ninth in offensive success rate through Sunday's games behind an improved rushing attack with David Montgomery and quarterback C.J. Stroud playing better. Stroud had 274 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. If that carries over, Houston is going to be good this season.

The Bengals' defense looked better. The Bucs' offense scored just 20 points and had fewer than 300 yards. Turnovers aren't guaranteed to carry over week to week but the Bengals forced four, including one that was returned for a touchdown. Cincinnati isn't going to be great on defense, but there have been some good teams to live off having a great offense and a defense that takes chances and makes a few game-changing plays. Maybe the Bengals can be that type of defense. That would be enough.

The overreaction directed at Drake Maye proves that the hate of the Patriots hasn't died just because Bill Belichick and Tom Brady are long gone. Maye didn't play well in the opener and didn't have a good postseason either. He played elite defenses in almost every game though. Maye is going to be good. He's just not able to overcome a middling supporting cast — A.J. Brown was out for the second half and TreVeyon Henderson was inactive in the opener — against great defenses as a third-year player. He's not nearly as bad as you'll read on social media.

The Bears are going to be fun to watch . The offense was fantastic against a Panthers defense that isn't great but not that bad (22nd in defensive DVOA last season). They put up 59 points, a franchise record for a season opener, and 552 yards. That's great. They also allowed 37 points and 478 yards against a Panthers offense that was 25th in DVOA last season. Every game might be a pinball machine. And the Bears' offense might be so good it doesn't matter how much the defense allows. It's why they're not higher in the top 10.

The Lions almost blew a 21-0 lead. They held on when they forced an incompletion on a 2-point conversion in overtime. Detroit's defense had played very well in building that lead, then let the Saints back in the game. Lions head coach Dan Campbell blamed the offense's inefficiency for the lead slipping away. "I'm like, man, we've got to be more efficient on offense," Campbell said . "We kind of spit and sputtered there and then they … had some tempo going."

The Lions face a very tough Week 2 game against the Bills, who will host their first regular-season game in their new stadium Thursday night.

The first look at new coordinator Sean Mannion's scheme wasn't great. Only the Steelers' offense had a lower success rate than the Eagles through Sunday's games. Jalen Hurts made some big plays, many of which were him creating something when nothing was open, and that saved the win. There's a long way to go for the offense.

Kenneth Walker III was excellent and will transform the Chiefs' offense. He had 173 yards rushing. Patrick Mahomes will be better as he get further removed from a torn ACL. He had just 184 yards passing and was off on many throws, but that didn't take away from a successful return. But one of the best stories of the opener was left tackle Kahlil Benson. He is an undrafted rookie out of Indiana who got no guaranteed money to sign with the Chiefs and did not play left tackle in college. He was forced into the lineup due to a Josh Simmons injury and there was rightful concern over him protecting Mahomes' blindside. But Benson, the first undrafted rookie to start Week 1 on the offensive line since Terence Steele with the Cowboys in 2020, played well and the Broncos rarely got any pressure on Mahomes. Offensive linemen don't get too much attention, but Benson deserves a lot of credit for stepping up when he had to.

The Jaguars were fantastic last season. There was nothing fluky about their season. Then they looked dominant in Week 1. They led 31-0 early in the third quarter and if they wanted to run it up, the final score could have been really ugly for Cleveland. Jacksonville was one of two teams in the NFL in the top six of EPA per play and EPA allowed per play through Sunday's Week 1 games ( Baltimore was the other). The Jaguars deserve respect.

Few teams looked better than the 49ers in Week 1. It remains to be seen how the 49ers react to coming back from Australia, but their next two games are at home against the Dolphins and Cardinals. That helps. It's hard to buy that the 49ers can stay healthy — exciting rookie De'Zhaun Stribling suffered an ankle injury that will keep him out at least a month — but if they can then San Francisco showed it can be as good as anyone.

We can't throw out everything we know because of one game. Maybe the Rams will be a huge disappointment this season, but it's too early to proclaim that. The Rams were the second-best team in the NFL last season and had a good offseason even before the Myles Garrett trade. Throughout the rankings, you'll see some teams that didn't move very much due to a great or bad Week 1. It's a one-game sample size for now.

Had it not been for the Bears, we'd be talking more about how good the Ravens' offense looked. They gained 502 yards, and that was with a conservative second-half approach after losing receivers Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane to injuries. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle was Ben Johnson's coordinator last season and the Ravens seem to have made a great hire with him. Keeping Lamar Jackson healthy is important, and the early receiver injuries are concerning, but the Ravens looked like a Super Bowl contender in Week 1.

More disrespect for the Seahawks to not be No. 1. Your anger is understandable, Seattle fans. But the Sam Darnold injury sets the Seahawks back a bit until he returns. But there's no question about Seattle's defense, which was excellent against the Patriots and carried the team to a win. Maybe that's enough to carry the team as long as Drew Lock is at quarterback.

Had Bills- Texans happened in prime time, as it should have, we'd be even more excited about what Josh Allen did against a very good Houston defense. The 36 points the Bills put up was the most against Houston since 2023, which was DeMeco Ryans' first season as head coach. Allen threw for 334 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for 23 yards and two touchdowns. That win was a statement. The fact that it happened in the 1 p.m. Eastern window just means the Bills won't get as much hype as they should. That might change Thursday night when they face the Lions.
